MIONTUAIRISCÍ DEN CHRUINNIÚ PLÉNACH DE CHOMHAIRLE
CHONTAE CHILL CHAINNIGH ARNA REÁLT AG LÚNASA, AN 20Ú LÚIL,
2026 AG 3.00 I.N. SA SEOMRA COMHAIRLE, HALLA AN CHONTAE
& TRÍ MS TEAMS
MINUTES OF PLENARY MEETING OF KILKENNY COUNTY COUNCIL
HELD ON MONDAY, 20TH JULY, 2026 AT 3.00 P.M. IN THE COUNCIL
CHAMBER, COUNTY HALL & VIA MS TEAMS
Chair: Cllr. Joe Malone.
Elected Members: Council Chamber
Cllrs. Tomás Breathnach, John Brennan, Jenny Catt Slattery, Mary Hilda
Cavanagh, John Coonan, Deirdre Cullen, Michael Delaney, Fidelis Doherty,
Maria Dollard, Michael Doyle, Patrick Dunphy, David Fitzgerald, Pat
Fitzpatrick, Joe Lyons, Andrew McGuinness, Eugene McGuinness, Seán Ó
hArgáin, Joe Sheridan and Maurice Shortall.
MS Teams
Cllrs. Brian Cleere, Ger Frisby, Michael McCarthy and Stephanie Doheny.
Officials: Lar Power, Martin Prendiville, Tim Butler, Mary Mulholland, Fiona Deegan,
Ian Gardner, Margo Hayes, Tony Lauhoff, Aileen McGrath, Richard Vaughan,
Eimear Cody, Frank Stafford, Mark McGarry, Catherine Cooney & Brenda
Kelly.
Fógraí - Announcements
Cathaoirleach Cllr. Joe Malone welcomed everyone and proposed that the meeting would finish at
5.00 p.m. to allow Elected Members attend funeral of Phil Hogan’s brother Paddy Hogan. This was
seconded by Cllr. Mary Hilda Cavanagh and agreed by all.
He requested Elected Members co-operation to ensure that Notices of Motion were dealt with before
end of meeting.
Cathaoirleach Cllr. Joe Malone congratulated:
▪ Cllr. Tomás Breathnach and Cllr. Seán Ó hArgáin who graduated from Maynooth University
completing a Spatial Planning Course in Maynooth through AILG.
▪ Cllr. Pat Fitzpatrick’s son-in-law Cllr. Daryl Barron on being elected as Lord Mayor of Dublin.
▪ Pia Langton, Molly Daly and Kate Maher who were selected to participate in the World U20
Championships.
He wished Henry Shefflin and David Herity all the best in their new roles with Kilkenny Hurling.
Cllr. Fidelis Doherty congratulated Linguan Valley on the success of the Mid Summers Night Festival
held in June. She also wished good health and happiness to Fr. Dan Cavanagh, brother of Cllr. Mary
Hilda Cavanagh who was due to retire after 52 years of service.
Cllr. Andrew McGuinness congratulated Jim Magner, Willie Byrne and team for organising a very
successful Festival in Castle Mills.
1
Vótaí Comhbhrón - Votes of Sympathy
Cathaoirleach, Cllr. Joe Malone together with the Elected Members extended votes of sympathy to the
following:
▪ Family of Patrick [Paddy] Hogan, brother of Phil Hogan
▪ Family of Ann Strappe, Mother of Breda Strappe, Housing Department
▪ Family of James Meadows, former employee of Kilkenny County Council and Father of Johnny
Meadows, Driver in the Thomastown MD
▪ Family of Con Daly, former employee of KCC – Tramore House Regional Design Office
▪ Family of Sean Barcoe, Father of Jason Barcoe, Human Resources Department
▪ Family of Paddy Morrissey, Father of Aidan Morrissey, Road Design Office
1. Dearbhú Miontuairiscí - Confirmation of Minutes
(i) Miontuairiscí Cruinniú Plé Ar Mheithimh - Minutes of June Plenary Meeting
Proposed by Cllr. Andrew McGuinness, seconded by Cllr. Seán Ó hArgáin and agreed:
“That Minutes of Plenary Meeting of Kilkenny County Council held on Monday, 15th June,
2026 as circulated with the Agenda be and are hereby approved”.
(ii) Miontuairiscí den Chruinniú Bliantúil - Minutes of Annual Meeting
Proposed by Cllr. Mary Hilda Cavanagh, seconded by Cllr. Andrew McGuinness and
agreed:
“That Minutes of Annual Meeting of Kilkenny County Council held on Friday, 26th June, 2026
as circulated with the Agenda be and are hereby approved”.
2. (a) Tithíocht & Díuscairt Eile - Housing & Other Disposal
(i) It was proposed by Cllr. Michael Delaney, seconded by Cllr. Mary Hilda
Cavanagh and agreed:
“That, in accordance with Section 183 of the Local Government Act, 2001, to dispose
of its interest in a vacant dwelling at Pollough, Kilmanagh, Co. Kilkenny (as identified
on the attached map) to Francis Morrissey and Agatha Zielinski Morrissey, Aprt Num
609, Zone 66, Building No 18, Street 51, Doha, Qatar for the sum of one hundred and
sixty thousand euro (€160,000) with each party responsible for their own legal costs
associated with the sale. The site area measures 1.186 acres/0.48 Ha. The Consent of
the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage is not required.”
2. (b) Pleanail - Planning
(i) Cuid 8 – Part 8: Paulstown Town Park Masterplan
Mr. Mark McGarry presented a PowerPoint Presentation and highlighted the
need to create a central point in Paulstown and connect all of the town’s
facilities and residential areas.
In his Presentation he gave an overview on the following:
▪ Site context and background.
▪ Aim is to create a community park with facilities for recreation, nature and
social activities.
▪ Two public consultation evenings were held.
▪ Five submissions were received, the details of which are included in the
Report.
▪ All submissions were taken on board as part of the finalised Masterplan.
The support of the Elected Members was sought to proceed with the
development.
2
Cllr. Pat Fitzpatrick thanked Mark for his presentation, noted the strong level
of public engagement and acknowledged both the value of the project and the
considerable detailed work that went into putting the Plan together.
It was proposed by Cllr. Pat Fitzpatrick, seconded by Cllr. Michael Delaney and
agreed that:
“We the Members of Kilkenny County Council approve the proposed Part VIII in
accordance with Section 179 of the Planning & Development Act 2000, as amended
and Part VIII of the Planning & Development Regulations 2001, as amended for the
proposed development of the Paulstown Park Masterplan, as circulated.”
(ii) Cuid 8 - Part 8: Clover Centre Masterplan [Attached]
Mr. Frank Stafford presented a PowerPoint Presentation in relation to the
redevelopment of the former Clover Centre lands as a multifunctional public
open space and community recreation facility.
In his Presentation he gave an overview on the following:
▪ Background of the site
▪ Public Consultations
▪ Proposed Development
▪ Seven submissions received, the details of which are included in the Report
▪ Key issues raised included amenity, trees and hedgerows, lighting, biodiversity,
heritage, Tidy Towns and site safety.
The support of the Elected Members was sought to proceed with the
development.
Contributions were received from Cllrs. Jenny Catt Slattery, Tomás Breathnach,
Pat Dunphy, Fidelis Doherty and Seán Ó hArgáin in relation to the following:
▪ Thanked Frank and his team for their excellent work and for engaging with
the people of Ferrybank and the surrounding area throughout the process.
▪ Expressed support for the project and satisfaction at seeing it progress.
▪ Welcomed the strong level of community engagement and the fact that
local views were reflected in the proposal.
▪ Acknowledged the workers of Clover Meats for their foresight in ensuring
the site remained in community ownership.
▪ Noted the important role the site has played in the life of Ferrybank and
welcomed its continued use as a community facility.
▪ Supported the inclusion of a dog park and suggested that a similar facility
should be considered within the City area.
It was proposed by Cllr. Jenny Catt Slattery, seconded by Cllr. Tomás
Breathnach and agreed that:
“We the Members of Kilkenny County Council approve the proposed Part VIII in
accordance with Section 179 of the Planning & Development Act 2000, as amended
and Part VIII of the Planning & Development Regulations 2001, as amended for the
proposed development of the Clover Centre Site Masterplan at Christendom Ferrybank,
as circulated.”
Mr. Tim Butler thanked Frank Stafford and Mark McGarry for their
Presentations and the work completed to date and noted that both projects will
be progressed through the URDF and RRDF funding streams.
3
(iii) Cuid 8 - Part 8: Age Friendly & Family Housing at Sr. Anthony's
(iv) Cuid 8 - Part 8: Group Home at Mallardstown Callan
Mr. Richard Vaughan presented a PowerPoint Presentation in relation to
upcoming Part 8 Planning Applications for Sr. Anthony’s, Lord Edward Street
and Group Home, Mallardstown, Callan.
In his Presentation he gave an overview as follows:
Sr. Anthony’s Site, Lord Edward Street
▪ Works started on first Pilot Houses including Reconfiguring layouts,
Compliant stairs, Energy retrofit and Garden upgrades.
▪ Next phase of Pilot Demonstration being developed to include 13 vacant
and occupied houses.
▪ Number of housing units.
▪ Due to be presented to the Council in November.
Group Home, Mallardstown, Callan
▪ includes 6 self contained, interlinked 1-bed units for people with profound
needs that are not suited to standard group home accommodation.
▪ Managed by Aurora Kilkenny.
▪ Due to be presented to the Council in December.
Contributions were received from Cllrs. David Fitzgerald, Seán Ó hArgáin,
Andrew McGuinness, John Coonan, Maria Dollard, Deirdre Cullen, Joe Lyons
and Joe Malone in relation to the following:
▪ Thanked Richard for his presentation.
▪ Fully supported both projects describing them as a significant step forward.
▪ Welcomed the progress of the Plan - pleased to see it coming to fruition.
▪ Noted that Sr. Anthony was the driving force behind the Butts and it was
fitting that the site would be used for community housing.
▪ Welcomed the strong involvement of the local community and praised the
consultation process as being well managed.
▪ Requested a copy of the Consultation Report to better understand how
public feedback influenced the final proposals.
▪ Described the project as a positive example of listening to communities and
developing solutions based on local views and ideas.
▪ Queried the layout proposed for Mallardstown, referring to a Swedish
model that combines private accommodation with shared community
spaces.
▪ Asked whether it was still possible to make a submission on the layout at
this stage.
▪ Requested that details of the project be advertised on the Council website.
(v) Tuairisc an phríomh-fheidhmeannach ar Athrú Molta Uimh. 10 - Plean
Iompar Uirbeach Inbhuanaithe
Chief Executive’s Report on Proposed Variation No. 10 - Sustainable Urban
Mobility Plan
Cllr. Malone proposed that this item be deferred to allow further discussion
and proposed the following Workshop and Meeting take place on Wednesday,
29th July, 2026 in the Council Chamber as follows:
3.30 p.m. Workshop to discuss Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan for
Kilkenny City.
4.30 p.m. Special Meeting to consider Chief Executive’s Report on
Proposed Variation No. 10 to Kilkenny City & County
Development Plan 2021 - Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan.
4
It was also proposed to hold a Workshop to discuss Differential Rents at 2.00
p.m.
This was seconded by Cllr. Pat Fitzpatrick and agreed by all.
(iii) Glacadh i gCúram/Taking in Charge: Friary Walk (Phase 3), Callan
It was proposed by Cllr. Michael Doyle, seconded by Cllr. Joe Lyons and agreed
that:
“We, the Members of Kilkenny County Council approve the initiation of proceedings
for the taking in charge of the following development in accordance with Section 11 of
the Roads Act, 1993 and in compliance with Section 180 of the Planning &
Development Act, 2000 as amended by Section 59 of the Planning & Development Act
2010”.
Development: TC199 - Friary Walk, (Phase 3), Callan, Co. Kilkenny
2. (c) Gnóthaí Corparáideacha – Economic Development
(i) Láthair ó Watershed - Presentation from Watershed
Mr. Tim Butler, Director of Services introduced Ms. Tina Dowling, CEO and
Donal Higgins, Chairperson to give an update on the Watershed.
Ms. Tina Dowling stated that she was proud to represent The Watershed and
highlighted the importance of recognising both the challenges faced and the
day to day operations required to ensure the facility continues to meet the
needs of the people of Kilkenny City and County.
She gave a presentation on the following:
▪ €20m invested by Kilkenny County Council.
▪ 600,000 visits every year.
▪ 47 staff.
▪ Operating for almost 18 years.
▪ Swimming, Sport, Fitness and Community Programmes.
▪ Supports schools, clubs and community groups.
▪ Safe, accessible, high-quality facilities.
▪ Membership grew from 848 in 2023 to 1,130 in 2026.
▪ One of the busiest public leisure facilities in the South East.
▪ Ongoing maintenance and upgrades.
▪ Biomass, solar PV and LED energy projects completed.
▪ Reducing costs and improving sustainability.
▪ A Valuable Community Asset.
▪ Training and competition venue for local Clubs.
▪ Sports and leisure opportunities for all ages and abilities.
Mr. Donal Higgins advised that the Board meets every six to eight weeks and
commended Tina for her transparency and the energy she brings to Board
meetings.
Contributions were received from Cllrs. Sean O’hArgain, John Coonan, David
Fitzgerald, Eugene McGuinness, Maria Dollard, Deirdre Cullen, Tomás
Breathnach, Andrew McGuinness and Pat Fitzpatrick as follows:
▪ Complimented staff and committee and the way they look after facility.
▪ Recognised the Watershed as a valuable facility, particularly its athletics
track, gym and swimming pool.
▪ Objective to cover cost has been maintained and managed.
▪ Schools Swimming Programme is exemplary.
5
▪ Athletics track great asset to young athletes.
▪ Is it possible to move towards 8 lane track to allow hosting of regional and
national athletics events given space constraints.
▪ Issue with closure of hydro therapy pool – no replacement meaning parents
with children with special needs have to travel to Waterford to assess hydro
therapy facilities – is this something that could be looked at.
▪ Facility for Kilkenny Aqua Kyak Club.
▪ Concern in relation to dressing rooms and infrastructure around pool and
gym.
▪ Noted requirement for long term reinvestment and capital funding plan to
remain sustainable.
▪ Additional sports facilities and suitable lands should be considered to meet
demand for activities not currently accommodated including cross-country
running and skating.
▪ Clarification was sought on accessibility and disability concessions.
▪ concerns were raised about affordability and the loss of regional events due
to costs.
▪ strong demand for a 25m pool with some users having to travel outside the
County to access services.
▪ costs can be prohibitive for some clubs and community groups.
▪ Improvement of access for community organisations.
Tina Dowling replied to queries and advised that providing a hydro-therapy
pool would require significant investment. The facility can fund day to day
operations and repairs but does not have the resources for major upgrades. It
offers reduced rates for groups including job seekers, students, people over 60
and carers as well as sensory hours.
Martin Prendiville advised that the Council recognises the challenges facing the
Watershed. The Capital Programme will be before the Council in September
where overall plan will be looked at.
(d) Airgeadas - Finance
(i) Ceathrú Mainistreach LDA - Abbey Quarter LDA
Martin Prendiville outlined the current position regarding the residential
development proposals within the Abbey Quarter. He advised that the
proposal involves a three way partnership between Abbey Quarter, Kilkenny
County Council and the Land Development Agency and discussions are
progressing to advance the planning process for residential development on
two sites within the Abbey Quarter.
Tony Lauhoff gave a Presentation and outlined the following:
▪ Residential development is proposed for Abbey Quarter sites at Plots 5 & 6
and Sweeney's Orchard.
▪ The project is being progressed through a partnership between Kilkenny
County Council, Abbey Quarter and the Land Development Agency.
▪ The Abbey Quarter has already delivered key projects including the Library,
Brewhouse, Public Realm works and proposed hotel development.
▪ Following the 2023 Masterplan review 35% of the site is designated for
residential use.
▪ Potential delivery of approximately 329 homes.
▪ A mix of social, affordable and cost rental housing options being considered.
▪ The LDA has been identified as a key partner due to its expertise, funding
capacity and role in delivering affordable housing.
▪ A coordinated development of all sites will support the long-term
sustainability of the Abbey Quarter.
▪ Both KCC and NTMA parties must consent to enter into agreement.
6
The support of the Elected Members was sought to the Partnership entering
into an Agreement between Kilkenny County Council, Abbey Quarter and
Land Development Agency to advance to planning stage for this development.
Martin Prendiville advised that the approval of the Elected Members is
required for the disposal of land under Section 183. He noted that the land to
be transferred at Sweeneys Orchard is uncertain at the moment as it will
depend on the mix of development.
The agreement of the Elected Members is sought to enter into a Memorandum
of Understanding with the Land Development Agency on the understanding
the land may need to be transferred to the LDA in the future if planning
permission is granted for the proposed development.
It was proposed by Cllr. Andrew McGuinness, seconded by Cllr. David
Fitzgerald and agreed that:
“Pursuant to Clause 5.5.2 of the Limited Partnership Agreement relating to Kilkenny
Abbey Quarter Development Partnership (original agreement dated 23rd December 2016,
amended and restated on 1st Oct 2024) between Kilkenny Abbey Quarter Development
Ltd, the National Treasury Management Agency and Kilkenny County Council, the
consent of Kilkenny County Council is required in respect of the disposal of any of the
Properties as defined in the said Limited Partnership Agreement. Clause 2 of Schedule 4
of the associated Shareholders Agreement (original dated 24th November 2016, amended
and restated on 1st October, 2024) further requires that such consent is required for “…the
entering into of any contract, agreement or understanding (whether legally binding or not)
so to do.
For the purposes of Cl 5.5.2 of the amended and restated Limited Partnership Agreement
and Schedule 4 of the amended and restated Shareholder Agreement, Kilkenny County
Council hereby consents to Kilkenny Abbey Quarter Development Partnership entering
into an Agreement with the Land Development Agency to advance a proposal to planning
stage for the development of plots 5 & 6 of the Abbey Quarter for residential and ancillary
uses on the understanding that in the event of a successful planning permission, all or part
of Plots 5 & 6 will be disposed of to the Land Development Agency for the purposes of
developing the plots for residential and ancillary uses, subject to conditions to be agreed
between Kilkenny Abbey Quarter Development Partnership and the Land Development
Agency.”
It was proposed by Cllr. Andrew McGuinness, seconded by Cllr. David
Fitzgerald and agreed that:
“Kilkenny County Council consents to entering into an Agreement with the Land
Development Agency to advance a planning application for the development of
residential accommodation and associated car parking on the site known locally as
Sweeneys Orchard in Kilkenny City, subject to conditions to be agreed between
Kilkenny County Council and the Land Development Agency.
This approval is given in the knowledge that in the event of planning permission being
granted for the proposed development, Kilkenny County Council will be required to
agree to a disposal of all, or part of, Sweeneys Orchard to the Land Development Agency
for the purposes of developing the site for residential and associated car parking use
(excluding any lands required for the development of social housing). It is further noted
that the required land disposal will be considered in due course by Kilkenny County
Council in accordance with the provisions of Section 183 of the Local Government Act,
2001 if and when planning permission has been granted and the extent of lands to be
disposed of is known”
7
Cllr. Seán Ó hArgáin expressed his concern stating that significant decisions
should not be made without thorough consideration and examination by
Members.
Cathaoirleach requested that a site visit to the Abbey Quarter be arranged for
Elected Members in September where all questions could be raised.
(e) Gnóthaí Corparáideacha – Corporate Affairs
(i) Tuarascáil Mhíosúil an Phríomhfheidhmeannaigh
Chief Executive’s Monthly Report
It was proposed by Cllr. Andrew McGuinness, seconded by Cllr. John Brennan
that the Chief Executive Report will be taken as read and this was agreed by
all.
Cllr. Deirdre Cullen welcomed the planning application for Kilkenny's
Riverside Water Sports Activity Facility. She queried the status of the
Feasibility Study for Riverside Amenity Area and pedestrian bridge in
Bennettsbridge. She noted that the Study has now been completed and
expressed a desire to see it progress. She also highlighted the need to further
explore opportunities along the River Nore particularly in terms of making
greater use of the area's natural amenities and facilities.
Cllr. Maria Dollard raised concerns in relation to polling cards being sent to
deceased relatives and asked if information could be provided on how to have
deceased persons removed from the Electoral Register.
Cllr. Dollard also requested that each Department provide a quarterly update
outlining the progress on the actions identified in the Biodiversity Action Plan.
(ii) Daingnigh Cathaoirleach don SPC 2 - Appoint Chairperson to SPC 2
It was proposed by Cllr. Deirdre Cullen, seconded by Cllr. Andrew
McGuinness that
“That Kilkenny County Council hereby appoints Cllr. Michael Delaney as Chair
designate to SPC 2: Transportation Policy/Mobility Management & Infrastructure”.
(iii) Coinne le Comhpháirtíocht Ceannaireachta Chill Chainnigh
Appointment to Kilkenny Leader Partnership
It was proposed by Cllr. Andrew McGuinness, seconded by Cllr. Michael Doyle
and agreed:
“That Kilkenny County Council hereby appoints the following Elected Members to the
Board of Directors for Kilkenny Leader Partnership:
Cllr. Pat Dunphy
Cllr. Pat Fitzpatrick
(iv) Cuairt Chlóite ar Minnesota - Twinning Visit to Minnessota
It was proposed by Cllr. Joe Malone, seconded by Cllr. Michael Doyle and
agreed that Cllr. Andrew McGuinness, Mayor would travel to Minnessota in
September.
3. Comhfhreagras - Correspondence
None.
4. Gnó ar athló ó chruinniúroimhe seo - Business adjourned from a previous Meeting
None.
8
5. Dátaí agus Amanta do chruinnithe a shocrú - Fix Dates & Times of Meetings
(i) Sceideal na gCruinnithe - Schedule of Meetings
This was noted and agreed by all.
6. Plé ar Thuairiscí agus Moltaí ó Choistí an Comhairle
Consideration of Reports & Recommendations of Committees of the Council
None.
7. Gnó Eile romhainn i bhFógra reachtála an Chruinnithe
Other Business set forth in the Notice convening the Meeting
None.
8. Oideachas agus Oiliúint - Education & Training
(i) Sceideal Comhdhálacha - Schedule of Conferences
Schedule of Conferences was noted.
9. Gnótha ag éirí as Miontuairiscí - Matters Arising from Minutes
None.
10. Aon Ghnó Eile - Any Other Business
Ms. Margo Hayes reminded Elected Members of the Workshop to discuss Standing Orders on
Monday, 7th September, 2026 at 3.30 p.m. and advised that there was a copy of Standing Orders
available to take away with them.
11. Fógraí Rúin - Notices of Motion
21 (26) Cllr. Eugene McGuinness
It was proposed by Cllr. Eugene McGuinness, seconded by Cllr. Maurice Shortall and agreed
by all:
“That Kilkenny County Council call on the Minister for Finance (the Tánaiste) and the Taoiseach to
abolish the Universal Social Change (USC). It should be noted that the USC was brought in as an
temporary emergency revenue-raising measure during a time of financial crisis, a crisis that our
Government now believes to be over and as such should fulfil their promise to totally abolish this charge
and put the money back in the pockets of the hard pressed tax payers of this country.”
Cllr. Seán Ó hArgáin spoke against the motion stating that Ireland is not a high tax economy.
He stated that lower taxes result in lower levels of public services and suggested that Ireland
should follow the Scandinavian model where higher taxes fund better services and facilities.
A roll call vote was taken on the proposed amendment and:
Twelve (12) voted in favour: Cllrs. Brian Cleere, Michael Doyle, Joe Lyons, John Brennan,
Maurice Shortall, Maria Dollard, Joe Malone, Eugene McGuinness,
Jenny Catt Slattery, Fidelis Doherty, Pat Dunphy and Ger Frisby.
Five (5) voted against: Cllrs. Joe Sheridan, Pat Fitzpatrick, John Coonan, Seán Ó hArgáin
and Tomás Breathnach.
Three (3) abstained: Cllrs. Deirdre Cullen, David Fitzgerald and Andrew McGuinness.
As majority voted in favour the Motion was carried.
9
22 (26) Cllr. David Fitzgerald
It was proposed by Cllr. David Fitzgerald, seconded by Cllr. John Brennan and agreed by all.
“That Kilkenny County Council prepare a road realignment scheme in conjunction with transport
infrastructure Ireland for the N.76/N.77 from Kilkenny City at the Castlecomer/ Ring road roundabout
through Dunmore Village, Hennebrys Cross, Conahy and onto Ballyragget to address the serious traffic
and road safety issues along this important busy National route”
Cllrs. David Fitzgerald, John Brennan, Pat Fitzpatrick, Seán Ó hArgáin and Andrew
McGuinness spoke in favour of this Motion.
Ms. Mary Mulholland advised that this road is not included for realignment under the
National Road Network Investment Plan and is not listed as a TII Improvement Project. The
matter can be raised with the TII, however, no repair works can proceed without TII's
agreement and approval.
23 (26) Cllr. Maurice Shortall
It was proposed by Cllr. Maurice Shortall, seconded by Cllr. Andrew McGuinness and agreed
by all:
“That Kilkenny County Council write to the Minister for Culture, Communications, Media and Sport,
Patrick O'Donovan TD, to call on him to urgently intervene following the collapse of Tickets.ie, which
has left a number of independent music festivals across Ireland facing significant financial difficulties.
The Council further calls on the Minister to engage with affected festivals, artists, performers and
creative workers to ensure that independent artists are paid in full for work undertaken and to provide
appropriate support measures to protect Ireland's independent arts and festival sector. Kilkenny
County Council recognises the vital contribution that independent artists and festivals make to our
cultural life, local economies and communities and expresses particular concern for those artists and
creative workers in Kilkenny who may be adversely affected by this situation.”
Cllrs. Maurice Shortall and Andrew McGuinness spoke in favour of this Motion.
24 (26) Cllr. Maurice Shortall
It was proposed by Cllr. Maurice Shortall, seconded by Cllr. Pat Fitzpatrick and agreed by all.
“That Kilkenny County Council write to Uisce Éireann, requesting that it immediately publish a clear
timeline for the planned water capacity works in Castlecomer. Residents in Castlecomer, Clogh and
Moneenroe have been living in unacceptable conditions, with water supplies being interrupted for up
to 16 hours a day over the past month. This level of disruption is having a serious impact on households,
families, older residents, and businesses, and is simply not acceptable in 2026.
The people of Castlecomer deserve certainty regarding when these long-promised capacity works will
commence and be completed. Kilkenny County Council should therefore call on Uisce Éireann to
urgently provide a detailed timetable for the delivery of these essential infrastructure works and to keep
the community fully informed throughout the process.”
25 (26) Cllr. Tomás Breathnach
It was proposed by Cllr. Tomás Breathnach, seconded by Cllr. Seán Ó hArgáin.
“That Kilkenny County Council write to the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
to seek the introduction of guidelines for solar farms to ensure they adhere to the highest standards, give
guidance to all involved in the planning process and set out the criteria for proper planning and
development by which they can be assessed.”
10
12. Fógraí i dtaobh Rúin ó Údaráis Áitiúla eile ag lorg tacaíochta ó Chomhairle Chontae Chill
Chainnigh - Notices of Motion from other local authorities seeking support of Kilkenny
County Council
It was agreed by all that the following Notices of Motion be taken as read and noted:
12 (26) Limerick City & County Council
“We will move at the next Meeting of Limerick City and County Council that this Council call
on the Minister for Finance to review personal taxes and the Universal Charge with effect from
January 20287 when presenting National Budget Legislation this October and that our sister
Authorities nationwide be requested to support this Motion.”
13 (26) Galway County Council
This Council agrees that the Comprehensive Economic Trade Agreement [CETA] providing
additional rights to multi-national corporations to sue the state outside of ordinary legal
systems we currently have will undermined EU social, health and environmental standards.
This Council acknowledges that many of the trade elements are already in place and does not
need the addition of corporations being able to sue the Irish government through the Investor
Court System [ICS] when any new laws affect their profits. This Council stands against the
Investor Court System [ICS] and calls this constituency a CETA-Free Zone. This Council
resolves to write to the Minister for Trade, the Minister for Local Government and the
Taoiseach to outline this position. It further resolves to publicise the Council’s concerns about
CETA and to circulate this motion with other Councils as correspondence for consideration.”
14 (26) Longford County Council
“We call on Longford County Council to write to the relevant Ministers, Fáilte Ireland, and
the City and County Management Association to implement an extension scheme to retain the
Just Transition Tourism Activators, who continue to support over 80 projects and their County
Tourism Officers, for a further period of 3-5 years to ensure the sustainable development of
tourism and the delivery of long-term economic benefits to transitioning communities. We
further call on Longford County Council to write to all local authorities within the Just
Transition Territory, and nationally, to support this motion in recognition of the critical
importance of continuity in delivering a successful Just Transition.”
15 (26) Clare County Council
“That Clare County Council notes the Government’s announcement of its cost-of-living
measures and expresses concern that the package unveiled does not meet the needs or wishes
of the Irish people. This Council calls on the Government to bring forward a fair and
comprehensive cost-of-living package that delivers meaningful relief for households, workers,
farmers and businesses. Please circulate this motion to the Taoiseach, Tánaiste, Minister for
Finance, all Oireachtas Members for Clare and Councils in the State.”

“In recognition of the cost-of-living crisis and that workers are suffering the most and

4. The report refers to benefits such as improved staff collaboration, reduced travel between
offices, increased organisational efficiency and improved working conditions. How were
these benefits assessed and quantified within the business case, and how will the Council
measure whether these anticipated benefits have actually been achieved once the building
is operational?
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
The fragmented locations and spread of staff across multiple sites does not create a cohesive
organisation. By consolidating four offices spaces into one, this will naturally improve staff
collaboration, reduced travel between offices, increased organisational efficiency and
improved working conditions. In the Final Business Case (FBC), this has been quantified using
research from Matrix Leadership Networks and Human Synergistics Australia that provide
frameworks for understanding and improving organizational culture. Staff Turnover, Wasted
Time, Rework, Stress and Absenteeism have an economic impact on an organisation through
inefficiencies linked to suboptimal working environments which could represent up to 29.35%
of payroll cost at the lower bound of estimates. For the FBC, it is recognised that not all of
these efficiencies will be realised in practice therefore the consultants have been prudent to
only used 25% of the 29.35% potential Organisational Efficiency and Productivity Benefits, to
calculate the Efficiency Savings.
These benefits can be measured through KPIs such as staff retention rates, Travel and
Subsistence costs and sick leave metrics.
5. What are the Council's long-term plans for the existing Civic Offices at The Glen and any other
buildings that will become surplus to operational requirements? Have potential disposal
values or alternative uses already been factored into the financial appraisal?
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
Should the proposed Civic Offices project proceed, The Glen offices and adjoining lands will
likely be sold on the open market. The decision to progress the proposed Civic Offices project
doesn’t affect the operations of any other Council owned property. However, MCC have
identified other properties that are surplus to operational requirements that could be
disposed of. Valuations have been obtained for three properties that could potentially be
disposed of, including the Glen offices and site.
These potential disposals proceeds have not been factored into the financial appraisal.
However, the proceeds from sale of surplus assets will be used to fund an additional
contingency of €1.7m for this project, if required.
If The Glen site were to be developed for housing purposes, the Council would benefit from
additional LPT income. A conservate estimate of additional LPT income is included in the
operational variance figures in the FBC. Refer to table 11.
6. Can the executive confirm if the proposed borrowing will have any impact on:
• Current capital projects planned across the county?
• Our ability to deliver on our roads programmes?
• Our ability to deliver our social and affordable housing targets?
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
Borrowing of €38m at 3.3% fixed interest rate over a 30-year term equates to an annual loan
repayment of €2.09m. The current annual provision of €1.5 million plus the expected cost
savings of €648k leaves a surplus of 58k after annual loan repayments.
Therefore, it is envisaged that the proposed loan repayments for the proposed Civic Offices
would not have an adverse impact on capital projects, our ability to deliver on our roads
programmes or our ability to deliver our social and affordable housing targets.

8. Having considered the procurement process, financial appraisal, economic appraisal and the
independent evaluation of the tenders, could you summarise for members and the public
why the Executive is recommending that this Council proceed with Tender 2, and why it
believes this represents the best long-term investment for County Monaghan?
Response from the Executive (Capital Projects):
While Tenderer 3 achieved the highest score under the Price criterion, the tender did not
achieve equivalent scores under the Quality criterion. In contrast, Tenderer 2 submitted a
more comprehensive and project-specific technical proposal, demonstrating a stronger
understanding of the project requirements, site constraints, delivery methodology and risk
management approach.
The Evaluation Team considered that Tenderer 2's submission provided a greater level of
confidence in the ability of the tenderer to successful delivery the project in accordance with
the Employer's Requirements. When both the Price and Quality assessments were combined
in accordance with the published MEAT evaluation methodology, Tenderer 2 achieved the
highest overall score and was therefore identified as the Most Economically Advantageous
Tender.
The evaluation was not based solely on the lowest tender price; rather, it was based on the
combination of price and quality criteria that had been established and published before
tenders were received, ensuring a fair, transparent and robust procurement process.
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
• The “do minimum” option still requires significant financial investment and would still not
provide a fit-for-purpose facility.
• One of the major operational costs, rent would continue to increase over time to a
conservative projected annual cost of €1.48m (including inflation) in 30 years' time.
• A fixed interest rate loan can be obtained from the Housing Finance Agency which
provides certainty over future repayments. The burden of this repayment reduces over
time due to inflation and expected growth in the Revenue budget.
• Proceeding with the new civic offices project represents a Benefit Cost Ratio of 1.8,
indicating that the benefits of the project outweigh the associated costs in comparison to
the Do Minimum option.
• MCC would fully own a strategic asset in 30 years' time, when the loan is repaid.
• This major investment in a key local authority asset would realise economic benefits for
Co. Monaghan, as set out in the Final Business Case.

FG Party Questions – Q1 to Q15 ('FG Questions')
1. In addition to retrofit capital costs of at least €12m for the Glen offices, can a best estimate
be made on the financial impact a retrofit would have on operating costs such as the need
to relocate staff for a prolonged period of time; additional rents, lost productivity, reduction
in delivery of services?
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
If the Glen site was fully vacated for the retrofit, 120 staff would have to be temporally
relocated. Market enquiries indicate finding rental space for 120 staff, with customer facing
facilities, disabled accessibility, parking and adequate IT infrastructure is not readily available
in Monaghan Town.
Estimating a two-year retrofit for relocation of staff with rental cost based on existing rental
charges incurred by MCC for rental office space (subject to availability) and estimated IT costs:
If there was a phased retrofit this would somewhat ease the challenge of finding rental space
for 120 staff at once, however finding rental accommodation for approximately 60 staff on a
phased basis, would be very challenging in the Monaghan town area. Other challenges include
continuity of services, IT infrastructure considerations, reduced meetings space and staff
engagement along with increase in travel expenses. Also phased construction would increase
construction costs due to additional health and safety provisions required to protect staff and
public while works take place and facilitate public-facing operations.
2. How disruptive would a retrofit of the Glen offices be operationally?
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
As outlined in Q1 FG Questions above, there are potentially two options; fully vacating The
Glen or implementing a phased vacation of the building. Both options would be highly
disruptive to the 120 staff currently based at The Glen, as well as to members of the public
who use our services.
Business continuity would be significantly affected, with staff experiencing considerable
challenges in carrying out their roles effectively. Market enquiries indicate that there is
currently no suitable alternative office accommodation available that could facilitate either
the full or partial relocation of staff from The Glen. A retrofit programme would further
increase the dispersal of staff across multiple locations, creating additional operational
challenges. Furthermore, the limited availability of meeting facilities and public-facing space
would have a direct impact on service delivery and staff's ability to conduct their work
efficiently.
There would also be significant challenges relating to IT infrastructure. Our IT servers are
currently located on site, and a retrofit project would present substantial logistical difficulties
in maintaining uninterrupted IT services throughout the works. Relocating the servers would
incur significant costs and could increase the risk of service disruption during the transition
period.

Permitted Increase Threshold has been set at 5% in the Form of Tender and Schedule. This

of corporate assets no longer required by the Council.
14. Is the current poor state and restricted space of the Glen offices a factor in employees
working from home and will the new offices encourage more employees to work in the
office?
Response provided by the Executive (Corporate Services):
Remote working in Monaghan County Council is governed by the Council’s Blended Working
Policy, which sets out how and when staff may avail of remote working, and is not driven by
the condition of any particular office building. Staff attendance patterns reflect how the
organisation operates, with attendance influenced by a combination of operational
requirements, blended working arrangements, and normal workforce factors such as annual
leave, flexi-leave, business leave, off-site work and inspections. These factors apply
consistently across the organisation regardless of the office location.
This is supported by attendance analysis across different Council buildings. Data from more
modern facilities, including Carrickmacross Civic Offices, shows similar typical and peak
attendance levels to those observed in the Glen offices. This indicates that attendance patterns
are consistent across locations and are not determined by the physical condition of a particular
building.
The purpose of the proposed Civic Offices is not to change or remove blended working, but to
provide a modern, accessible and fit-for-purpose workplace that better supports
collaboration, service delivery and staff wellbeing when staff are on-site. While an improved
environment will enhance the overall workplace experience and support engagement,
attendance levels will continue to be determined by operational needs and agreed working
arrangements. Ongoing engagement with staff and unions will continue to ensure that these
arrangements are clear, balanced and support both service delivery and staff wellbeing.
11
15. Will the new office cater for assumed employment growth or will we have to rent additional
office space?
Response provided by the Executive (Corporate Services):
The proposed Civic Offices have been designed to accommodate both current staffing levels
and projected growth over time, without the need for additional rented office space. At
opening in 2029, the building will provide 260 desks for a projected staff of approximately 275,
which reflects a modest staff-to-desk ratio of approximately 1.06 to 1. This is appropriate given
established attendance patterns, where 80-85% of staff are typically on-site at peak, equating
to approximately 220-235 staff, meaning desk capacity will operate at around 90% utilisation
with a small buffer available.
Looking ahead, projected staffing levels are approximately 290 by 2034 and 305 by 2039. The
initial desk provision remains workable through the early years, with peak utilisation increasing
gradually but remaining manageable. The building has been deliberately designed with
internal expansion capacity to 306 desks, which is expected to be activated at around 305 staff,
ensuring that peak demand continues to be accommodated without the need for external
accommodation.
On this basis, the design provides a planned and scalable solution to staff growth. It ensures
that the Council can accommodate future workforce requirements within the building itself,
while avoiding the cost and inefficiency of over-providing space at the outset. The approach
balances current operational needs with long-term flexibility and removes the need to rely on
additional rented office space under the projected growth scenario.
Questions from Cllr PJ O’Hanlon Q1 to Q10 ('Cllr O'Hanlon Questions')
1. Monaghan County Council currently employs 380 indoor staff. The new offices accommodate
300, where will the surplus be accommodated?
Response provided by the Executive (Corporate Services):
The figure of 380 indoor staff refers to the Council’s total current indoor workforce across all
services and locations. The proposed Civic Offices are designed to accommodate those staff
who will relocate to a central administrative headquarters, which is approximately 260
currently. The remaining 120 staff are not part of this relocation cohort, as they are based in
operational and service locations such as libraries, museum and cultural services, fire and civil
defence, and the three Municipal Districts. In terms of capacity, the Civic Offices would open
with 260 desks, which aligns with the current relocating staff base and supports projected
growth through blended working arrangements. Peak attendance patterns show that typically
80–85% of staff are on-site at any one time, equating to approximately 220–235 staff at
opening, meaning the building will operate at around 90% desk utilisation on peak days, with
a buffer available. As staffing grows over time, the building has planned internal expansion
capacity to 306 desks, which will be activated when required, ensuring that future demand
can be accommodated within the building. On this basis, there is no surplus of staff requiring
alternative accommodation, as the Civic Offices are designed specifically for the cohort of staff
who will relocate, with a capacity model that reflects how the organisation operates in practice
and a clear pathway to scale as required.
2. Have the working practices for the new building been agreed with staff?
Response provided by the Executive (Capital Projects and Corporate Services):
Yes. Staff have been actively involved throughout the design and workplace planning process
for the proposed Civic Offices. Workplace engagement has been an ongoing component of the
project and has informed both the building design and the proposed workplace strategy.
Engagement with staff has taken place through a number of channels, including:
• Leesman Workplace Survey completed by staff to inform the Workplace Strategy.
• Civic Office Project Staff Committee, comprising 14 staff representatives.
12
• Staff workshops and presentation sessions open to all staff.
• Interviews with Heads of Section to understand operational and service delivery
requirements.
• Civic Office Steering Committee, including 7 staff representatives from across the
organisation.
• Presentations to the Senior Staff Forum.
• Benchmark visits by staff representatives to modern office buildings to review workplace
layouts and working practices.
While the overall workplace strategy has been developed through this engagement process,
staff engagement will continue throughout the construction phase, should the project
proceed. This will ensure that staff are kept informed and have opportunities to contribute to
the detailed planning and implementation of workplace practices in advance of occupation of
the new building. It is worth noting that, in addition to ongoing local engagement, under
Section 2.5 (Workplace of the Future) of the Public Service Agreement 2024 to 2026, it was
agreed at public sector wide level that staff will cooperate with new ways of working, including
blended working arrangements. This reflects the need to have more agile, digitally-enabled
and collaborative workplaces,
3. What has been the growth of staff employment over the past 3 years (year on year)?
Response provided by the Executive (Corporate Services):
The year-on-year staff growth over the past three years (excluding retained fire-fighters),
based on figures captured in July of each year to ensure a consistent comparison, is as follows:
staffing increased from 436 in 2023 to 461 in 2024, an increase of 25 staff or 5.73%; from 461
in 2024 to 470 in 2025, an increase of 9 staff or 1.95%; and remained unchanged at 470
between 2025 and 2026, representing 0.00% growth. These figures demonstrate that recent
growth has been variable, with a higher increase followed by a more moderate increase and
then stabilisation. It is important to place this pattern in context. The higher growth in the
earlier period reflects a phase of post-COVID catch-up recruitment and the expansion of
services, including areas such as Community (LA Integration Team, Local Community Safety
Partnership, Community Support Workers), Town Regeneration, Communications, and
expanded Housing function. For long-term planning purposes, a 1% annual growth assumption
has been applied as a prudent steady-state baseline. This avoids sizing a long-term capital
investment on the basis of short-term fluctuations, while still allowing for organic growth over
time. It provides a balanced approach and ensures that long-term accommodation planning
remains proportionate and sustainable.
4. Page 50, table 11, the rental saving of €14.667 million over 30 years. On the previous page
there is a rental cost of €359,000 per annum that can be avoided. 30 x 359,000 = €10.77
million. This is a difference of €3.897 million. Are these figures correct?
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
The €359,000 rental costs are based on 2025 expenditure. In the FBC, the rental costs are
anticipated to increase annually due to an estimated 1% increase in staff over the next 30 years
and the impact of inflation. The increase in rental cost due to the estimated increase in staff
numbers combined with inflation results in a forecast annual rental payment of €1.48m in year
30. The cumulative rental cost over 30 years is forecast at €24.2m.
5. On page 12, point 2 it estimates €1.56 million to €5.2 million per annum in additional local
spending from staff and visitors. How was this calculated?
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
In line with the Infrastructure Guidelines the additional local spend estimates are indicative
and assumption-based and subject to displacement, leakage and substitution effects. As such,
they are not included in the core NPV calculation and they are presented to illustrate local
economic significance only.
13
While these benefits are not included in the core cost-benefit calculation, they nonetheless
represent a significant additional contribution to the local economy, reinforcing the strategic
and socio-economic justification for the project. Economic impacts were estimated using a
standard gross-to-net additionality framework. The assessment first estimates gross local
expenditure associated with employee spending and visitor expenditure. The resulting
expenditure is then considered in the context of potential leakage, displacement and
substitution effects and a conservative local expenditure multiplier. This approach is consistent
with recognised public sector appraisal guidance including the Infrastructure Guidelines and
the Additionality Guide methodology.

Indicative local economic impacts were estimated using a gross-to-net additionality
framework. Gross local expenditure was derived from the estimated staff payroll associated
with the proposed Civic Offices and an assumed proportion of spending retained within the
local economy. The assessment acknowledges that not all expenditure represents net
additional economic activity and that impacts may be reduced by leakage, displacement and
substitution effects. Consistent with recognised appraisal practice, a conservative expenditure
multiplier of 1.3 was applied to illustrate the wider circulation of spending within the local
economy. These estimates are presented as indicative local economic impacts only and are
not included within the core economic appraisal or NPV calculation.

6. Page 45 section 6, everything is really based on estimates and assumptions, we have seen
many public expenditure projects run over budget (e.g. BioConnect and Peace Campus). How
accurate are these estimates?
14
Response provided by the Executive (Capital Projects):
Construction Cost Allowances
The tendered construction cost comprises
Office Building: €27,622,198
External Works: €5,225,501
Totalling the tendered construction value of €32,847,700.
Current construction inflation is estimated at approximately 2–3% per annum. The
contractor's tender includes an allowance that absorbs the majority of anticipated inflation
over the construction period. In addition, the project budget includes a separate allowance for
inflation under the Price Variation Clause, bringing the total inflation provision to
approximately 6% over the planned two-year construction programme. A Contingency
Allowance of €1,527,646 (approximately 5% of the contract value) has been included to cover
any unforeseen employer requirements, necessary project changes or other unexpected costs
that may arise during construction. This level of contingency is in line with normal industry
practice for projects of this scale and complexity and was recommended by the project's Cost
Consultants. In addition to the €1,527,646 contingency built into the tender report and
recommendation, the Executive propose and recommend that an additional ‘Corporate
Contingency’ of €1,757,524 is put in place, to provide an overall contingency of 10% of the
proposed Civic Offices building costs. The additional Corporate Contingency would be funded
through the sale of corporate assets no longer required by the Council. A further Direct Costs
Allowance of €500,000 has been included to cover project-related costs not contained within
the construction contract, including Monaghan County Council project management and
administrative costs.These allowances represent prudent financial management and are
intended to minimise the risk of future budget overruns. The project is being delivered using
the PW-CF2 Public Works Contract (Building Works Designed by the Contractor), which
transfers a significant proportion of design and quantity-related risks to the contractor and
therefore reduces the Council's exposure to cost uncertainty during construction.
7. Car Parking - How many car parking spaces are provided for parking? Have we rented out
spaces from other sources? Who are the providers? How many spaces are there? What is the
annual cost?
Response provided by the Executive (Capital Projects):
A total of 239 parking spaces would be available to serve the proposed Civic Offices. This
provision comprises:
• 114 new on-site parking spaces to be constructed as part of the proposed Civic Offices
project; and
• 125 additional parking spaces secured through an agreement with Monaghan Harps GAA
Club at an annual rental cost of €8,000.
This approach was selected following an assessment of alternative parking options. The
principal alternative was the construction of a multi-storey car park. However, this option
would have involved a significantly higher capital cost and was not considered to represent
good value for money.
The adopted parking strategy will provide 239 parking spaces at an estimated cost of €1.615
million (€6,757 per space), compared to an estimated €4.577 million (€26,924 per space) for a
170-space multi-storey car park. Accordingly, the agreed parking strategy delivers a greater
number of spaces at a substantially lower overall cost and represents the most cost-effective
solution for the project.
15
8. I was happy to hear at the last Co. Co. meeting that assets that are not being used will be
sold. Is it possible that the monies from these sales would be given back directly to the
ratepayers who are funding this new project?
Response provided by the Executive (Finance):
The proceeds from the sale of assets would be used either to fund additional corporate
contingence contingency for the proposed Civic Offices project, referred to earlier, and if the
additional contingency is not required, it would be used to fund capital projects or unfunded
capital balances.
9. In relation to the BioConnect building project, would it be possible to defer the
commencement of the building of the new offices to see how the BioConnect building
performs? The last thing we need is another vacant building.
Response provided by the Executive:
It is recommended that the commencement of the construction of the proposed Civic Offices
would proceed should the Members give their approval for the project to proceed to the
construction phase. Separately, the Council is working proactively with public and private
sector partners to ensure the completion, occupation and operational readiness of the
BioConnect facility.
10. Is Monaghan Co.Co. satisfied that this new building will cater for all its needs for the next
thirty years?
Response provided by the Executive (Corporate Services):
Yes. Monaghan County Council is satisfied that the proposed Civic Offices are designed to meet
the organisation’s long-term operational needs, incorporating modern standards, flexible
workspace design, and capacity to support hybrid working and future service demands. The
building has been future-proofed to allow for growth and adaptation over time; however, as
with any long-term projection, ongoing monitoring of workforce trends and service
requirements will be necessary to ensure continued alignment over the full 30-year period.

That the council, in conjunction with Waterways Ireland, install public bike repair

The motion was proposed by Councillor Durkan and seconded by Councillor Clear.
