Self Help Grant Scheme
The following motion in the names of Councillors Suzanne Doyle, Anne Connolly,
Brian Dooley and Veralouise Behan was considered by the members.
That the council ring fence funds realised through the Housing Allocation Deposit
scheme to support the roll out of the Self Help Grant scheme.
The motion was proposed by Councillor Doyle and seconded by Councillor A
Connolly.
A report from Ms A Aspell, Director of Service, Housing and Corporate Services
stated that the Tenant Deposit Scheme was adopted in 2018 and came into effect in
January 2019. At the cessation of a council tenancy, and subject to certain
conditions, the deposit is refundable; it is important that the income from this fund is
available for the refund of deposits or in dealing with the cost of turning around
properties which become vacant and where the damage is in excess of normal wear
and tear. Adequate funding is required to deal with future liabilities, and it is
anticipated that refunds will increase in future years. Details of the Tenant Deposit
Scheme are appended.
The members decided during the Budget 2022 process that the funding which had
previously been allocated to the Self-Help Scheme would be re-allocated to the
Disabled Persons Grants Scheme. This additional funding was used to leverage an
increase in funding provided by the Department of Housing, Local Government and
Heritage, with total funding increasing from €517,504 in 2021 to €1,062, 775 in 2022.
The Self-Help Scheme provided an allocation for staff funding, as a result of the
decision to suspend the scheme this resource was re-allocated, currently no staff
resources are available to administer the scheme.
I acknowledge that there is merit in the motion, however in advance of any decision
on the future funding of the Self-Help Scheme it is recommended that the scheme is
reviewed by the Housing Strategic Policy Committee, with any review to include an
examination of the resourcing of the scheme, the value of the grant being made
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 7 of 19
Kildare County Council
available, the type of works being granted funded and the possibility of using monies
from the tenant deposit scheme to support the scheme.
Councillor Doyle appreciated the report and stated she was cognisant of the
resources it would take to effect the action being sought, and proposed that once all
the DPG grants were processed, work on the self help scheme applications could
commence. She clarified that the funding to be used was from the deposits on
housing allocations and that consideration should be given to commencing work on
the suspended Self Help Grant scheme applications first.
Ms Aspell stated she supported the motion in general terms but asked to be given
time to assess the implication on resources and the potential for staff reassignment
and how that would be managed.
Councillor Doyle understood the points being made but added that a full review of
the matter would take too long, and sought the members support to the motion.
Resolved on the proposal of Councillor Doyle, seconded by Councillor A Connolly
with 24 members voting in favour of the motion, no member voting against the
motion and with one abstention, the motion was approved.
13/0422
Unauthorised Developments
The following motion in the names of Councillors Bernard Caldwell, Michael
Coleman, Naoise Ó Cearúil, Daragh Fitzpatrick, Paul Ward and Carmel Kelly
was considered by the members.
That the council receive a report from Planning/Development Control on the number
of reported unauthorised developments over the past three years and that this report
include details of the date first reported, how many are still in the system that were
reported prior to March 2019, what the current status is on files and what level of
resources are required to service this activity. Furthermore that the council
recommend actions or requirements to improve mechanisms to deal with this activity
more effectively.
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 8 of 19
Kildare County Council
The motion was proposed by Councillor Coleman and seconded by Councillor
Caldwell.
A report from Mr E Ryan, Director of Service, Planning, Strategic Development and
Public Realm stated that the level of detail requested in the motion will take a
considerable amount of time and resources to compile. The issue of resourcing is a
matter for the Executive. However, it should be noted that resourcing levels within
all Planning Departments are currently being reviewed and examined at a national
level through the CCMA and LGMA.
Councillor Coleman stated the response was inadequate and asked that the matter
be included for discussion again the following month. He referenced a report the
Celbridge-Leixlip committee had received recently on this matter which had been
much more detailed. However, he did acknowledge that resources were stretched in
the Planning department.
Following a discussion, the members raised the following points:
• The issue had come up at a Naas MD committee meeting also, and an
example was given of an Order to Demolish that was due to be served in the
Naas Municipal District Committee area in September 2021 but had yet still to
be served.
• Was the Director of Planning in the process of sourcing additional resources
for the Planning Department.
• The Director was asked for any update on resources from his work on the
Working Group with the OPR on analysing resourcing around the country etc.
and whether there would be any appetite at national level to subdivide the
enforcement function so that a fine system could be introduced on lesser
breaches, as a separate process to the planning process which was a very
lengthy and labour-intensive process.
• Clarification was again sought on the availability of the online UD system and
why it had been removed from the council’s website
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 9 of 19
Kildare County Council
• Was there any form of prioritisation given to UD files and consideration be
given to members being briefed in the triage process as they were bearing the
brunt of the public disquiet on the council’s inaction in this area.
• Who was liable to pay costs if local residents took an injunction on a UD case.
The Director responded by acknowledging the comments made by the members. He
asked for the detail of the files referenced in the Naas area and stated he would look
into the position re the online UD system online. He noted that a report had been
made available by the OPR and that new staffing resources would be a matter for
the CCMA. He outlined the various vacancies that currently existed in planning and
where they were at within the recruitment process. He noted that the court system
was a very cumbersome process and that he has had discussions around innovative
ways of dealing with and prioritising UD cases. He noted that once a case gets to the
court, the onus is always on the local authority to prove the case and not the other
way around. He noted that individuals taking an injunction was a private matter, and
that they would be responsible for the costs involved. He concluded by confirming
there would be a further update to the motion given in the Progress Report for the
May meeting.
Resolved on the proposal of Councillor Coleman, seconded by Councillor Caldwell
and agreed by the members present, the report was noted and an update to be
provided in the following months Progress Report.
14/0422
Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change report
The following motion in the names of Councillors Aoife Breslin, Fintan Brett, Íde
Cussen, Noel Connolly, Aidan Farrelly, Ciara Galvin, Noel Heavey, Colm Kenny,
Nuala Killeen, Vanessa Liston, Pádraig McEvoy, Peggy O'Dwyer, Rob Power and
Evie Sammon was considered by the members.
That the council outlines how key scientific findings of the Intergovernmental Panel
on Climate Change report (4 April 2022: CO2 420.69 ppm) will inform and be
addressed by policies and climate action across the local authority services,
including but not limited to energy conservation, public realm, sustainable transport,
biodiversity and planning.
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 10 of 19
Kildare County Council
The motion was proposed by Councillor McEvoy and seconded by Councillor
Breslin.
A report from Mr J Boland, Director of Services, Water Services, Environment and
Climate Action stated that it is fully accepted that there are very significant
challenges for the local government sector arising from climate action and, indeed,
this is reinforced in the report cited in the motion. These matters can be discussed in
detail as part of the quarterly standing item on Climate Action which is included in the
main agenda. It will be noted that there are many ongoing initiatives at local level
which will have to be further deepened and mainstreamed both in terms of services
and policies, as suggested in the motion. There was no question but that climate
action is now having a very significant impact across all departments. In this context,
the support of the elected members to date, particularly through the CPG, SPCs,
MDs and full Council really had to be acknowledged. Directors would be in a position
to address any detailed questions relevant to specific services or policies relating to
their departments.
Councillor McEvoy acknowledged the report but stated that as policy makers, the
local authority had to demonstrate it was having due regard to the climate crisis. He
noted that Irish citizens were responsible for three times the level of emissions that
other EU residents were. He asked that an urgency be brought to this work given the
critical juncture the crisis was at. Councillor Liston asked that more visibility be given
to what we as an authority are doing versus what was expected of us, and that the
council needed to be more ambitious in its approach.
Mr Boland welcomed the motion and the members comments stating that Climate
Action had to be interwoven through all services delivered by the local authority. He
also noted that strategic collaboration and business initiatives were going to be key
in the area, adding the council had come a long way in this area.
Mr Ryan stated the Climate Change document was quite technical but that the
planning department would welcome any submissions made during the CDP review
process by experts in any area relevant to the report.
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 11 of 19
Kildare County Council
Resolved on the proposal of Councillor McEvoy, seconded by Councillor Breslin and
agreed by the members present, the report was noted.
15/0422
JAM (Just a Minute)
The following motion in the name of Councillor Tracey O’Dwyer was considered by
the members.
That given Kildare County Council, is a JAM (Just a Minute) friendly organisation can
additional signage be placed at all public counters informing customers that council
staff are trained to facilitate customers requiring this service.
The motion was proposed by Councillor T O’Dwyer and seconded by Councillor P
O’Dwyer.
A report from Mr M Hurley, Health and Safety and Access Officer stated that the
Access Officer, will liaise with facilities team to arrange the placement of additional
signage informing customers that the council is a JAM Friendly organisation.
Councillor Tracey O’Dwyer welcomed the report and asked that the signage around
the Áras be enhanced. She also asked for confirmation that Kildare County Council
was listed on the JAM website as a JAM friendly organisation.
Ms Wright undertook to establish whether the council was listed as a JAM Friendly
organisation on the JAM website.
Resolved on the proposal of Councillor T O’Dwyer, seconded by Councillor P
O’Dwyer and agreed by the members present, the report was noted.
16/0422
Waste Management Review
The following motion in the name of Councillor Kevin Duffy was considered by the
members.
That the council provide an update on the Waste Management Review that was to
be undertaken, including the standardisation of litter management across our urban
centre.
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 12 of 19
Kildare County Council
The motion was proposed by Councillor Duffy and seconded by Councillor Clear.
A report from Mr J Boland, Director of Services, Water Services, Environment and
Climate Action stated that by way of background, the Council currently spends
€2.525m on street sweeping and litter bin emptying as per the 2022 budget book. All
in all, it is considered to be a good service with, for example, Naas having been
deemed the cleanest town in Ireland in 2022 by IBAL, (Leixlip was 4th). In addition,
this county is now only second to Cork County in the Tidy Towns medal league table
with 10 medals.
He outlined that this matter had been the subject of a series of reviews/assessments
in very recent times, including -
1. A general review culminating in a detailed report of street cleaning operations
by the Council’s Senior Executive Engineer.
2. A survey of physical litter related infrastructure (copy attached) as requested
by the SPC.
3. Lengthy consideration of all litter/street cleaning issues by the SPC as part of
consideration of the new Litter Management Plan.
4. Compilation of a draft policy/protocol on litter bins, again at the request of the
SPC (copy attached).
5. Further broader consideration of all relevant litter related issues by full Council
in 2021 in the context of the Covid emergency.
He further confirmed the following outcomes to date -
• A key recommendation of the A/Senior Engineer was the rationalisation of
services in respect of the Naas MD area wherein the service will shortly (likely
to be May 2022) be taken over in full by the Roads Dept. This will mean that
all litter/street sweeping operations will rest with one department
(Transportation). This also accords with the recommendations of the SPC.
• The draft “Street Litter Bin – Installation Policy” (copy attached) is still with the
SPC for final endorsement. In particular, the SPC have asked for further
consideration regarding the possible achievement of greater consistency of
bin provision throughout the county. In the view of the undersigned, such
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 13 of 19
Kildare County Council
could only be realistically achieved over time. Indeed, I would also suggest
that, in line with climate action / sustainability considerations that the policy
could also reflect an objective to reduce the overall number of bins, again over
time.
• A further, more focused review was carried out in conjunction with the Covid
emergency wherein these matters were debated at full Council. Following the
confirmation of national grant funding, additional weekend street sweeping
was put in place at key pinch-points for the last summer period (cost
€84,000). Furthermore, some additional bin infrastructure was also provided,
through this grant, mainly (though not exclusively) in conjunction with public
realm projects.
On a general note, it was never intended that reviews/interventions in this area
would be “forensic”. In this context it is always open to the MD Engineer to effect
local efficiencies either in relation to street sweeping or litter bins where such makes
sense. There will also be instances where there is local agreement regarding new
bins being provided where there is good reason, subject to underutilised extant bins
being removed (also refer to draft policy).
The members will also need to appreciate that this is a very labour intensive and
expensive service wherein, in truth, it has been very difficult to control expenditure in
light of the myriad of demands. Accordingly, any requests for additional services
would need to be carefully costed and considered in the context of the annual
budgetary process. In particular, any suggested ‘reviews’ should not be interpreted
as an opportunity for yet more bins and/or additional street sweeping.
Playgrounds are serviced separately by the Parks Department by contract following
a tender. I can discuss possibilities for synergies with that department following
expiration of this contract though, realistically, I suspect that the MD Engineers are
unlikely to have the capacity to take on such an additional task.
Finally, the ongoing voluntary effort of local tidy town groups really had to be
acknowledged in this discussion. He stated that other Directors may also wish to
comment.
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 14 of 19
Kildare County Council
Councillor Duffy welcomed the report noting the difference in the processes that had
been outlined relating to playgrounds and cemeteries. He stated a conversation
would have to be held again at budget time, adding he would like to see more
rationalisation of the bin collection service and the budget. Councillor Hamilton
supported the motion stating society in general had become lethargic and had fallen
into bad habits on the issue, and the council needed to re-engage with businesses
and community groups in relation to rubbish and waste disposal.
• Following a discussion, the members raised the following points:
The suggestion of phasing out bins was completely disagreed with, as having
more bins mean less rubbish.
• Kildare is an expanding county and an equitable method of distributing
resources related to bins and bin collection, had to be found
• The 7-day bin collection that operated during Covid and worked really well
and should be continued.
• Towns and town public realm spaces were being utilsed more since covid,
especially at weekends, and could the collection days be examined with a
view to having them at peak times such as weekends, as opposed to earlier
weekdays when it was quieter.
Mr Boland thanked the members for their comments noting the Naas MD office
would be taking over the bin collection service in the Naas area in the near future.
He stated that the SPC still had a body of work to do in researching and considering
this matter.
Councillor Duffy welcomed the feedback from the members noting the inconsistency
of approach across the MDs had to be addressed, and that the council should look at
the emerging technology in the sector that could guide it where to allocate its labour
resources.
Resolved on the proposal of Councillor Duffy, seconded by Councillor P O’Dwyer
and agreed by the members present, the report was noted and and it was agreed the
motion would be referred to the Environment,Water Services and Climate Action SPC
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 15 of 19
Kildare County Council
17/0422
Walking and Cycling Strategy for the County
The following motion in the name of Councillor Bill Clear was considered by the
members.
That Kildare County Council develops a Walking and Cycling strategy for the county.
The motion was proposed by Councillor Clear and seconded by Councillor Killeen.
A report from Ms E Wright, Director of Service, Roads, Transportation and Public
Safety stated that Objective TM A5 of the Draft County Development Plan sets out
that it is an Action of the Council to Prepare a walking and cycling strategy to identify
and invest in new high-quality, suitable, safe, and sustainable walking and cycling
routes, in consultation with stakeholders with links from towns and villages to public
transport services, amenities, services, schools, and existing and proposed
developments. These walking and cycling routes should be segregated and the
cycling routes should accommodate two-way access, whenever possible. The
Sustainable Transport Section is implementing the Greater Dublin Area Strategic
Cycle Network in the County, which involves improvements for all vulnerable road
users (pedestrians/cyclists) in consultation with the National Transport Authority.
Councillor Clear stated he was delighted to see this item in the County Development
Plan given that Kildare had the most Greenway and Blueway development in the
country. Councillor Keatley stated that the Roads department were also looking at
cycle rack facilities for rural schools.
Ms Wright stated the council had set out the NTAs 2022 programme under active
travel, and the councils biggest challenge would be to deliver that programme. She
confirmed that the issue raised by Councillor Keatley was being looked at by TII
along with how to ensure that road users are aware they are using a shared space
ie. cars, walkers and cyclists. Ms Wright confirmed a monthly update was given on
all active travel projects in the monthly Chief Executives report. She also confirmed
the active travel team would be making a presentation to the municipal district
committees twice yearly.
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 16 of 19
Kildare County Council
Resolved on the proposal of Councillor Clear, seconded by Councillor Killeen and
agreed by the members present, the report was noted.
The Cathaoirleach noted the next item on the agenda was a motion in the name of
Councillor McLoughlin Healy, who was not in attendance. He stated he was not
aware that anyone had been authorised in writing to move the motion on her behalf
thus on that basis and in accordance with Standing Orders, the motion fell.
19/0422
Progress on EV charging
The following motion in the name of Councillor Peter Hamilton was considered by
the members.
That the council provide an update on the progress made since the Local Authority
Guidelines on EV charging and electric vehicles were issued in August 2021 and
specifically outline what improvements in capacity can be made at our 'destinations'
in advance of the summer 2022 tourism season.
The motion was proposed by Councillor Hamilton and seconded by Councillor
Liston.
A report from Ms E Wright, Director of Service, Roads, Transportation and Public
Safety Department stated that The Roads, Environment, EM CARO would
collectively review the recently published strategy by Minister for Transport Eamon
Ryan - Ireland’s first national EV Charging Infrastructure Strategy. Chapters 5
(Pathway to Delivery), Chapter 6 (Infrastructure Delivery) and Chapter 7
(Implementation) are of note and the Department is inviting views on the strategy.
This draft Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Strategy 2022-2025 sets out the
Government’s ambition regarding the delivery of a public electric vehicle charging
network to support up to 194,000 electric cars and vans on our roads by 2025. It
describes the four main types of charging that will form the basis of our network:
• Home/apartment charging
• Residential neighbourhood charging
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 17 of 19
Kildare County Council
• Destination charging
• Motorway/enroute charging
It also sets out a plan for the delivery of each of these in the coming years, based
upon partnerships between the Department of Transport and a range of relevant
stakeholders, including industry, private charge point operators, local authorities and
citizen drivers. The Department is currently inviting views on the draft strategy to be
submitted to evinfrastructure@transport.gov.ie A formal public consultation will be
run by the Department in May consisting of an online survey and stakeholder
workshops. A representative of the Roads Department will participate in a
forthcoming Stakeholder Engagement on EV infrastructure delivery and fleet
management as part of the consultation on the draft Strategy.
Councillor Hamilton acknowledged the report noting his motion was connected to the
joint motion that had been debated earlier in the meeting in relation to the Panel on
Climate Change Report. He stressed the importance of local leadership and the
need for the council to proactively work on and advance this issue. He noted that
both the public and the private sector had a role to play, adding that private charge
rates were very expensive compared to a night charging rate, in a home.
Ms Wright stated the private sector had a key role to play in this area noting the
council has had engagement with EV providers. She did however confirm that no
funding has been assigned by Government in this area to date and even if there was
funding, public procurement procedures would have to be followed. She confirmed
the council was monitoring all Government advances in this area, but highlighted the
lack of funding was a critical issue.
Resolved on the proposal of Councillor Hamilton, seconded by Councillor Liston and
agreed by the members present, the report was noted.
The Cathaoirleach confirmed this concluded the business of the meeting. He stated
he was conscious of the cost associated with running the plenary council meetings in
Newbridge Town Hall and expressed the desire that these meetings would be able to
return to the council chamber soon. He thanked all the staff in Facilities, Security and
Minutes of Kildare County Council meeting 250422 Page 18 of 19
Kildare County Council
Corporate Services and the sound system provider for their invaluable input and
support over the course of the pandemic in enabling the council meetings to operate
in Newbridge Town Hall.
The meeting concluded.

Minutes of the Ordinary Meeting of Galway City Council
held on Monday 11th March 2019
at 3.00pm in City Hall, College Road, Galway.

Presiding: Cllr. N. McNelis, Mayor of the City of Galway.
Present: Councillors: Councillors: B. Cameron, C. Connolly, C. O Conchuir, P.

Conneely, M.J. Crowe, O. Crowe, M. Cubbard, F. Fahy, M. Farrell, P.
Flannery, P. Keane, N. Larkin, M. Lohan, D. Lyons, D. McDonnell, T.
O'Flaherty, and J. Walsh.

In Attendance: Mr. B. McGrath, Chief Executive
Mr. T. Connell, Director of Services

Note: The Minutes of the Meeting and Agenda Items are recorded in the order of their
consideration.

The Mayor commenced the meeting at 3.00pm with a proposal to suspend Standing Orders, in order
to continue a workshop on the Large Scale Sports Infrastructure Fund. The Mayor advised that the
Council Meeting would formally recommence at 3.30pm. This was proposed by Cllr. O. Crowe, and

The Council Meeting recommenced at 3.30pm with a statement of intention to conduct the business

The Mayor thanked Members for facilitating the suspension of Standing Orders, and proposed to
progress through the Agenda as follows: Item 1(a); 2(a); 2(b) with 4(j); 2(c); 3(a); 3(b) and 4 (d); and
A(c). The Mayor would then take Items 4 (b) (f} (g) (h) (i), and (k).

Mr. B. McGrath drew Members attention to item 7.2 — Proposals to Modernise the Electoral

advised that she had submitted a number of questions by email regarding Item 4, and understood

That councillors may submit questions to the Executive for written response in relation to all |
| Agenda items debated and discussed at City Council Meetings to provide clarity and transparency.

Not considered.

Item 2(a) Event Licensing Report for the St Patricks Day Parade under Section
238 of the Planning Act for consideration at the Council meeting of 11th
March 2019

Mr. L. Blake, Senior Executive Planner, outlined the Event Licence Report for the St Patrick’s Day
Parade, under Section 238 of the Planning Act. The application was advertised on 1* February 2019
in the local and national press and was received on the 4" February 2019. The closing date for
submissions was 21° February 2019, three weeks after the public notices. No third party submissions
had been received from members of the public by 21% February 2019.

1|Page
The event entails a Parade from NUIG Quadrangle, University Road, passing over the Salmon Weir
Bridge, through Courthouse Square, Eglinton Street, Williamsgate Street and Eyre Square North,
finishing at Prospect Hill, and involving performers and floats on St Patrick’s Day, Sunday 17° March
2019, between the hours of 11.30am and 1.00pm. The event is expected to attract an audience of up
to 30,000, and will be a free non-ticketed event for members of the public.

Queries from Councillors included:

Parking management; Parade Director; updates on Galway City Council website; change of route;
Cross Street/ Shop Street works; flags/ dress code for parade; Litter management; funding for
parade; Community wardens; wheelchair platform; bus diversions; free public transport;
participation of Galway2020; voluntary closure of off licences; mobile toilets; length of route;
notification re change of route; banners on Shop Street; use of schools for park and ride facilities;
and Irish language/ music in the parade.

Clarification was provided in response to queries raised. Mr. L. Blake noted Members’
disappointment re the change in route, but advised Members that the risk of having building
materials and a builders enclosure on the route was too high, with works planned on Shop/ Cross
Street ongoing. Banners would be erected as requested, and Event Organisers would be asked to
look at the inclusion of Irish music/ Irish language. Mr. B. McGrath committed to comprehensive
parking management along the route of the parade, and advised that the parade route could not be
publicised until the event licence was granted by Members.

Proposed: Cllr. M.J. Crowe Seconded: Cllr. D. Lyons

Item 2(a) Proposal to Grant Event Licensing for the St Patricks Day Parade under Section 238 of the
Planning Act.

In Favour: 16 Against:0 Abstain:0 Present: 16

The Motion was passed.

Cllr. M. Cubbard submitted a motion regarding provision of free public transport for St Patrick’s Day.
Mr. B. McGrath advised members to make provision for a budget for free public transport or park
and ride in September 2019, with a view to implementing in 2020.

Cllr. D. Lyons proposed that the Executive would look at the costs involved before budget time, and
report on same. Cllr. M. Cubbard amended the original motion. Members voted on the amended
motion, as below.

| Proposed: Cllr. M. Cubbard Seconded: Cllr. C. Connolly

| propose Galway City Council explores a free public transport service be provided between the

Item 4(j) Proposed Prohibition on Election Posters.

Mr. G. McMahon advised Members that a motion relating to Election Posters was passed at the
November 2018 Ordinary Meeting, as follows:
“In supporting a cleaner and safer environment, Galway City Council commits to develop and
implement a bye-law prohibiting the use of election posters or the posting of any type of
politically motivated election material on public facilities or in publicly controlled spaces
throughout the Galway City area subject to legal advice”.

This motion was referred to Galway City Council’s Law Agent for legal advice. A number of statutory
elements refer, including Litter Pollution Act 1997, amended by the Electoral (Amendment) (No. 2)
Act 2009; Protection of the Environment Act 2003; Planning and Development Regulations 2001 as
amended; European Parliament Elections Act 1997; Local Elections Regulations 1995; Referendum
Act 1994 and the Electoral Act 1992. The Litter Pollution Act, 1997 specifically exempts the
distribution of election material and allows for the erection of posters and other material under
particular controls regarding their placement and the periods allowed following the signing of an
election order.

Mr. G. McMahon advised that the Motion as passed in November could not be implemented as a
bye-law, as it was addressed by National legislation. Mr. G. McMahon acknowledged Galway County
Council, which had given permission for a comprehensive reply on the same topic to be circulated.
At present, there are no mechanisms by which the Executive of Galway City Council could enforce a
prohibition on election posters. However Members could agree to a voluntary code.

Cllr. P. Flannery read NOM 06/19, which relates to this Item. Members discussed the motion and the
use of election posters.

Queries raised by Councillors included:

Quantity of signs that will be in use in May; accidents/ insurance; use of other means of advertising;
compliance with a voluntary code of conduct; plastic ties; composition of posters; recycling of
posters; outdoor designated area.

1. Justification

1.1 Lack of demonstrated benefit

The proposed eastern bridge location does not clearly demonstrate a benefit to
the vibrancy of the town centre or to the effective flow of active travel. It is not

Chief Executive's Prelimina

The CE does not support the

evident how this proposal would encourage movement into the commercial core
or support existing businesses.

1.2 Land use and connectivity

The eastern landing point at South Quay is primarily residential in nature and does
not represent a strong destination. In contrast, a western crossing would connect
more directly with established commercial areas, including cafés, pubs and other
town centre uses, and.would better align with existing movement patterns.

1.3 Impact on heritage

There are concerns regarding the impact on the setting of the Nineteén Arches
Bridge, a structure of significant historic importance and a defining feature of
Arklow. The introduction of a new bridge in close proximity would risk detracting
from its visual setting and the character of the river corridor.

1.4 Navigation constraints

The Avoca River is an active navigation channel, including use by yachts and
leisure craft. The siting of a bridge in this location would present constraints in
terms of clearance, span and navigation, which require careful consideration.

1.5 Flood relief considerations

It is noted that the Arkiow Flood Relief Scheme is currently being advanced. In this
context, the inclusion of a bridge objective at this stage is considered premature,
as it may interact with or onstrain the delivery of flood relief infrastructure. A
coordinated and integrated approach is necessary.

1.6 Alternative approach

Consideration should be given to the potential to enhance the existing bridge,
including widening and the provision of dedicated pedestrian and cycle facilities.
This approach could deliver active travel improvements without the need for a
new structure in close proximity.

2. Conclusion

The eastern bridge objective is not sufficiently justified, is premature, and raises
concerns in relation to heritage, navigation and infrastructure coordination.

| therefore recommend that the AT2 objective be removed from the easterly
location and reconsidered as part of a more integrated approach to future bridge
provision in Arklow.

1. Justification
1.1 Environmental sensitivity — Arklow Marsh

The proposed greenway would traverse or run adjacent to Arklow Marsh, a
‘proposed Natural Heritage Area (pNHA)’ of significant ecological value. This site
supports sensitive wetland habitats and a range of bird and plant species.

Under ‘EU Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC)’ and related national planning policy,
any development likély to affect the integrity of designated or proposed natural
habitats requires ‘Appropriate Assessment’ and mitigation. No such assessment
has yet been undertaken for the Laragh Greenway route.

Potential impacts include:

* Disruption of habitats and species

* Increased human pressure on a sensitive ecosystem

* Permanent alteration of wetland functions

1.2 Interaction with the Arklow Flood Relief Scheme

The greenway must also be considered alongside the ongoing ‘Arklow Flood
Relief Scheme’, -which involves major works within and alongside the river

corridor.
Including a greenway at this stage could:

* Conflict with flood relief infrastructure

* Require redesign or relocation later

19
* Increase cumulative environmental impacts on sensitive habitats

Until flood relief works are completed, the greenway objective is ‘premature’.
1.3 Existing and future greenway strategy

Wicklow is already progressing the ‘Arklow-Shillelagh Greenway’, which will
provide a high-value inland route linking Arklow with County Carlow.

Given this, a ‘preferred second greenway’ should focus on a ‘coastal route’,
linking South Wicklow to Wexford. A coastal greenway:

* Offers scenic and recreational benefits
* Avoids environmentally sensitive inland areas such as Arklow Marsh

‘

* Provides strategic connectivity along the coast without conflicting with flood
relief or protected habitats

1.4 Prematurity and policy alignment
The inclusion of the Laragh Greenway as a fixed objective is ‘premature’, given:
* The environmental sensitivity of Arklow Marsh

* Its status as a pNHA

* The ongoing Arklow Flood Relief Scheme
* The existence of the Arklow-Shillelagh Greenway project

A more considered approach would involve completing flood relief works,
undertaking detailed environmental assessments, and identifying routes that
avoid sensitive habitats while aligning with EU Habitats Directive obligations.

2. Conclusion

While the development of walking and cycling infrastructure is supported, the
Laragh Greenway, as curreritly proposed, raises significant environmental risks
and is inconsistent with EU and national habitat protection policy.

| therefore propose that this objective be removed from the plan at this stage,
with future greenway development focused on a ‘coastal route linking South
Wicklow to Wexford’ as a more sustainable and environmentally appropriate
alternative.

JUST TRANSITION Ms. A. Delaney informed the members that the Budget 2020
UPDATE provided for a suite of measures to support a just transition for
the Midland Region, noting the appointment of a Just
Transition Commissioner, provision for a Midlands Just
Transition Fund, the Midlands Deep Retrofit Programme and
the NPWS Bog rehabilitation programme. In addition to these
actions, the Midlands Regional Transition Team in partnership
with the Commissioner has progressed the technical assistance
programme provided by the START Team and has developed
a suite of skills / training measures.
She advised the members that Commissioner Mulvey’s first
progress report has been submitted to the Department and is
due to be signed off shortly. She noted that the report will
detail stakeholder engagement to date and will contain a
number of recommendations for the Minister and Government
to consider. She informed the members that the mechanism to
administer the Just Transition Fund in the amount of €6M with
a further €5M from ESB is currently being considered.
Ms. A. Delaney updated the members on the Midlands Deep
Retrofit Programme in the amount of €20m to be shared
amongst the 5 Counties (Laois, Longford, Offaly, Westmeath
& Kildare). She advised the members that a number of
meetings have been held with representatives from SEAI,
DCCAE, DoHPLG, OGP, Offaly, Westmeath, Longford, Laois
and Kildare County Councils to progress the Midlands Deep
Retrofit scheme and that a circular is to be issued to each Local
Authority outlining the parameters of the scheme which will
seek to bring dwellings to a minimum Building Energy Rating
of B2. She advised that the meetings held to date have
indicated that the scheme would allow for the upgrading of
between 150 and 200 units in each county, and would involve
two stages and two procurement processes, the first is the
survey/design works and the second, the
construction/upgrading works. She noted the timeline is
subject to Covid-19 restrictions and that his has been brought
to the attention of the Just Transition Commissioner.
Ms. A. Delaney outlined the NPWS Bog Rehabilitation
Programme in the amount of €5M with Bord Na Móna
appointed by the Department of Culture, Heritage and the
Gaeltacht as project managers to oversee the implementation
of restoration works on 9 raised protected bogs in the Midlands
region and to undertake the restoration works. She noted that
NPWS have indicated that this rehabilitation programme could
provide for up to 70 jobs in the Midland region across a range
of professions including machine operators, engineers,
hydrologists, ecologists, environmental scientists, site
supervisors, community liaison personnel and in evaluating
amenity development potential.
Ms. A. Delaney updated the members on the START
programme, a Holistic Plan for Just Transition in the Midland
Region and that the START team are currently finalising the
Socio Economic Profile of the Region. She advised that the
START Community engagement programme was initially
planned to host a number of workshops in the communities,
however given the current worldwide pandemic, these must
now progress through electronic means utilising existing LA
networks including the PPN, LEO newsletters and Local
Development Companies. The purpose of the community
engagement is to identify projects for delivery in the impacted
bog community areas. This will result in a prioritised project
inventory, focusing on identifying key, credible, considered
projects to facilitate change. This will, in turn, help to sign-post
potential future funding requirements and noted that work has
commenced on the Skills & Education Paper for the Region.
Ms. A. Delaney advised the members that Ireland is required
to develop a Territorial Just Transition Plan, for approval by
the European Commission, which will provide the overall
strategic framework for investments of the funding received.
She noted that the current understanding is that DEPR will lead
the negotiations for Ireland and this Fund will be part of the EU
Multi-Annual Financial Framework (MFF) 2021-2027, which
still has to be finalised. She advised that the funds will not be
available from this Fund until 2021 at the earliest.

operatives are fully au fait with the Nearly Zero Energy
Building Standard that has been introduced to the Building
Regulations. She outlined the various training schemes and
redeployment opportunities in development, with training

on location at various Bord Na Mona Works and associated
peatlands.

ii. The appointment of a beach warden – it was confirmed that no budget existed
for an appointment;
iii. The provision of bus shelters – it was agreed that Councillors should identify the
locations and this would be referred to the Transportation Section.
10 Any Other Business
• It was confirmed that a meeting with Oireachtas members and the Transportation Section
would take place on Thursday 18th December to receive an update on the Slane Bypass.
• Eugene Farrelly outlined the plan to use the proceeds from the cow plot rentals to fund a
grant scheme, with one-off match funding to be provided to community groups, with a
closing date in early January and to be launched in Lobinstown. This was agreed on the
proposal of Councillor Tom Kelly and seconded by Councillor Sharon Tolan. A report would
be presented to a future meeting.
This concluded the business of the meeting.
Signed:

Miontuairiscí / Meeting Minutes
Navan Municipal District
Ordinary Meeting
10:00 a.m., 23rd March 2016, Navan Civic Offices
An Meára, Councillor Joe Reilly, presided.
Councillors Present: Sinéad Burke, Francis Deane, Padraig Fitzsimons, Wayne Forde, Jim Holloway,
Tommy Reilly.

Apologies: Claire King, Meetings Administrator and Noel Finnegan, Executive Engineer.
Councillor Joe Reilly welcomed Councillor Padraig Fitzsimons to the meeting. He also thanked all
involved in the St Patrick’s Day Parade.
1 Confirmation of Minutes
1.1 Confirmation of minutes of Ordinary meeting held on 24th February, 2016.
The Minutes of the Ordinary Meeting held on 24th February, 2016 were adopted on the
proposal of Councillor Tommy Reilly and seconded by Councillor Francis Deane.

Sympathy was extended to:-
• The family of the late Tommy Grimes, former Member of Kells Town Council.
• Those who were killed in the recent attacks in Brussels.
• The family of the members of the McGrotty and Daniels families, who died tragically
in Donegal.
5 Statutory Business
5.1 Corporate Services
5.1.1 To receive a presentation on Event Management Guidelines.
Dara McGowan, Senior Executive Officer, Corporate Services delivered a
presentation on the event management guidelines, which included information
on procedures, event categories, pre-planning, risk management and
requirements.

benefit to groups organising events.
5.1.2 To note Municipal District Allocations submitted by Councillors on behalf of

Meath County Council Page 2 of 9 Corporate Services

the vacancy created following the election of former Councillor Shane Cassells,
to Dáil Éireann.
Councillor Padraig Fitzsimons was nominated on the proposal of Councillor
Tommy Reilly and seconded by Councillor Francis Deane. As there were no
other nominations Councillor Padraig Fitzsimons was appointed to the Board of
Navan Enterprise Centre Company Ltd.
5.2 Transportation
5.2.1 To receive a Progress Report on works undertaken/planned for Navan
Municipal District.
The report had been circulated in advance and was noted.
6 Notice of Question
6.1 Submitted by Councillor Sinéad Burke
“Can the Executive clarify the roles and responsibilities of both the Council and
the Department of Education & Skills when granting planning permission for
schools, specifically around suitable and safe traffic management plans for these
developments?”
Response:
In the first instance, the Department of Education & Skills (D.E.S.) will consult with the
planning authority in respect of any proposal they may have for a new school or for a
school extension. The D.E.S is formally advised of the issues which may need to be
addressed at pre planning stage in the context of any future planning application.
The Planning Authority remains as the decision maker in relation planning applications
for schools, in exactly the same way as it would for all other types of development.
Where additional traffic management infrastructure or signals are required, they may
be provided within or close to the school grounds or more likely on the surrounding road
Meath County Council Page 3 of 9 Corporate Services
Miontuairiscí / Meeting Minutes
network. The general rule of thumb is that traffic management improvements required
to enable a school will be delivered on foot of the development proposal or as a
condition of planning permission.
The cost of those works are either directly funded by the school body, where the works
are within the school development boundary, or are provided by the Local Authority in
the wider area and funded by a special development contribution imposed under the
terms of the planning consent.
The response was noted.
6.2 Submitted by Councillor Wayne Forde
“Does Meath County Council plan to carry out a feasibility study with a view to the
construction of a public walkover across the N3 for public access and safety from north
Navan to and from the town centre onto Abbey Road?”
Response:
It is presumed that reference is being made in this Notice of Question to the old N3
(R147). Regardless of this, there are no plans to look at the construction of a public
walkway at this location.
The response was noted. Councillor Wayne Forde asked that the Transportation
Department be asked if they would reconsider.
6.3 Submitted by Councillor Francis Deane
“What is the up-to-date situation with regard to the taking in charge process for the
Millbrook Estate in Johnstown?”
Response:
The Council can confirm that a list of outstanding remedial works for the satisfactory
completion of the development has issued to the receiver appointed to Hollioake Limited
(in Receivership) requesting a timeframe for completion of these works. To date The
Meath County Council Page 4 of 9 Corporate Services
Miontuairiscí / Meeting Minutes
Council has not received a response from the Receiver indicating a timeframe for the
completion of these works. The Council will continue its efforts to engage with the
receiver.
The response was noted.
7 Notice of Motion
7.1 Submitted by Councillor Wayne Forde
“Can I call on my fellow Councillors to fully support my motion of creating a memorial
garden within Blackwater Park dedicated to the memory of the many young people of
the town of Navan who have died tragically over the years and before their time.”
Supporting information subject to the motion being proposed, seconded and
considered:
The spirit of the Motion is fully acknowledged, but has to be considered in the context of
the need to develop a memorial policy and protocol regarding same, so as to ensure that
such current, and future proposals, are developed in line with an overall framework that
has been agreed by Meath County Council, which will also guarantee that the amenity
of our public parks are duly maintained.
The motion was proposed by Councillor Wayne Forde and seconded by Councillor
Francis Deane. A short discussion followed and it was agreed that the erection of a
stone/sculpture would be looked at in the overall context of developing the park.
The motion was adopted.
7.2 Submitted by Councillor Wayne Forde
“Can I call on the support of my fellow Councillors to support my motion of closing off
an alleyway in Ferndale between house numbers 142 and 143?”
Supporting information subject to the motion being proposed, seconded and
considered:
Meath County Council Page 5 of 9 Corporate Services
Miontuairiscí / Meeting Minutes
The closing of the walkway would result in an increased walking distance out of the
estate for 32 houses, the longest distance being 0.43km. This would be at variance with
the connectivity and permeability principles of sustainable residential environments and
the objectives of the Navan Transport Plan 2014 - 2019. The closing of the walkway
would also result in a “no man’s land”, which may become littered and overgrown and
may still attract anti-social behaviour. Any decision to consider the closing of the
walkway would require consultation with the residents.
The motion was proposed by Councillor Wayne Forde and seconded by Councillor Jim
Holloway. A short discussion followed with regard to connectivity and permeability and
Kevin Stewart advised that the Navan and County Development Plans will be coming up
for review and it would be worthwhile looking at such policies as part of this review.
It was agreed on the proposal of Councillor Sinéad Burke and seconded by Councillor
Wayne Forde to initiate the legal process involved in the extinguishment of the public
right of way.
The motion was noted.
7.3 Submitted by Councillor Francis Deane
“That Navan Municipal District work along with local community groups on the town's
litter black spots and strive towards improving our position on the litter league.”
Supporting information subject to the motion being proposed, seconded and
considered:
A Working Group has been established to look at litter related issues affecting Navan
and to come up with measures to eradicate litter black spots from the town. The Council
recognises and appreciates the very key role that Community Groups play in litter
eradication from our towns and villages and will work and support such groups in
whatever way possible in achieving this goal.
The motion was proposed by Councillor Francis Deane and seconded by Councillor
Wayne Forde.
The motion was adopted.
Meath County Council Page 6 of 9 Corporate Services
Miontuairiscí / Meeting Minutes
7.4 Submitted by Councillor Francis Deane
“That our town hall in Watergate Street will remain in the charge of Navan Municipal
District, holding on to the present counter services.”
Supporting information subject to the motion being proposed, seconded and
considered:
The town hall in Watergate Street will remain in the ownership of Meath County
Council, however all the staff will be based in Buvinda House. All the services currently
provided at the counter in Watergate Street will be provided in Buvinda House, as well

The motion was proposed by Councillor Francis Deane and seconded by Councillor
Sinéad Burke.
Councillor Joe Reilly enquired as to the future use of the building and asked it remain

Services.
The motion was noted.
8 Correspondence

The correspondence was noted.
9 Any Other Business
9.1 Councillor Sinéad Burke raised the following issues:
9.1.1 The relationship between the Superintendent or Probation Officer and Meath
County Council with regard to Community Service or Return to the Community
Meath County Council Page 7 of 9 Corporate Services
Miontuairiscí / Meeting Minutes
Scheme – it was pointed out that Meath County Council had been asked if there

Offaly County Council

Minutes of Special Meeting of Offaly County Council
Held on 23 March 2026 at 11.30am, in Aras an Chontae, Charleville Road,
Tullamore and via Teams

The Meetings Administrator carried out a roll call to confirm attendance.

Present

Clir. John Leahy, Cathaoirleach
Cllr. Bryant, Ollie Cllr. Murray, Claire (SF)
Cllr. Clendennen, Eleanor Cllr. Murray, Shane
Cllr. Cribbin, Noel Cllr. Murray-Smale, Claire (FF)
Cllr. Egan, Hugh Cllr. O’Brien, Sean
Clir. Feighery, Neil Cllr. Ormond, Peter
Cllr. Maher, Sean Cllr. Quinn, Liam
Cllr. Masterson, Aoife
Cllr. McDonnell, Fergus
Cllr. Moran, Frank

Apologies

Cllr D. Harvey, Cllr A. Hennessy Kennedy and Cllr E. Fitzpatrick.

Officials in Attendance

Mr. E. Ryan, Chief Executive; Ms. F. Millane, D.O.F.; Ms. A. Dillon, D.O.S.; Mr. B. Lennon, A/D.O.S.;
Mr. P. McLoughlin, D.O.S.; Mr. A. Murray D.O.S.; Austin Hickey Director BDO; Ciaran Brannigan
BDO consulting team; Mr. E. Fennell, Meetings Administrator; Ms. AM. Kelly, Administrative
Officer; Ms. E. Sutton, C.O

1. BDO Presentation

Mr. A. Murray, Director of Services, advised that this special in-committee meeting would include
a presentation from Austin Hickey and Ciaran Brannigan of the BDO consulting team on the
potential pooling of community development funds. Mr A. Murray first provided the elected
members with the presentation he delivered at the Offaly Green Energy Conference.

Mr. A. Murray outlined Offaly’s renewable electricity developments, progress to date,
infrastructural challenges and opportunities influencing the future of energy in the Midlands.

He advised that County Offaly is now the number one county in Renewables Generation
nationally. He advised that the Economic Development Strategy is now to harness this ‘pipeline’

1|Page
of c. 2GW of renewable energy developments to support the creation of jobs and to support
communities.

Mr. A. Murray reported that Offaly’s wind pipeline represents 11% of the national 9,000 MW target,
despite the county comprising only 2.3% of the State’s landmass. The County Development Plan
2027 wind target is 466 MW. For solar, Offaly’s pipeline amounts to 14% of the national 8,000
MW target, with a 2027 plan target of 145 MW.

He noted that Offaly’s combined renewable energy pipeline is now approximately 2GW and
highlighted the key challenge of securing economic and community benefits from this capacity
while maintaining the county’s long-standing commitment to managing the cumulative impacts,
supporting host communities appropriately, and protecting broader objectives in community
development, tourism, heritage, and biodiversity.

Mr. A. Murray advised that Offaly continues to lead in integrating amenity development with
renewable energy. He noted that while many sites traditionally had restricted access, the county
planning department ensured that Offaly’s first large-scale wind farm at Mountlucas (2014)
included significant public amenities, including a learning centre, the first wind-farm parkrun, a
sensory garden, and over 10 km of walking routes.

Mr. A. Murray noted the following in respect of the future benefits:
1. Pooling of RESS (Renewable Electricity Support Scheme) Community Benefit Funds.
2. Offaly’s proposed peatland reserves
3. Ensuring Renewable Energy Directive plans (RED III) and the Regional Renewable Energy
Strategy (RRES) work with the Offaly ‘pipeline’
4. Continue to progress the Midlands Cycling Destination in Offaly

Mr. A. Murray concluded by noting Offaly’s long-established role in national power generation and
highlighted the scale of current opportunities. He emphasised that the next priority is to ensure
this capacity translates into sustained economic development, alongside meaningful community
benefits and legacy projects that reflect Offaly’s contribution to national energy targets.

Cllr. J. Leahy, Cathaoirleach, thanked Mr. A. Murray for his presentation, and he introduced Austin
Hickey and Ciaran Brannigan of the BDO consulting team.

Mr. A. Hickey advised that the purpose of the presentation was to outline work undertaken on the
potential creation of an economic development and investment fund for Offaly. Over the past
nine months, he and his team have assessed the feasibility of pooling Community Benefit Funds
(CBFs) and other funding streams into a unified investment vehicle for Offaly.

He noted that, given the scale of wind-farm development in Offaly, such a fund could deliver
stronger strategic impact for both host communities and the wider county. Several key areas
were reviewed as part of this assessment. The key areas examined included stakeholder appetite,
legal and governance structure, operational models, eligible project types and fund scheme
design.

A briefing was provided on the Renewable Electricity Support Scheme (RESS) Community Benefit
Funds (CBFs), noting the fund size, purpose, examples of eligible uses and governance. He
advised the scheme aims for 80% renewable electricity by 2030 and requires all supported
projects to establish a Community Benefit Fund. It also provides mandatory annual payments to
households within 2km of wind farms.

2|Page
Mr. A. Hickey outlined the implications for Offaly which included approximately 1.5 GW of
operational or planned renewable projects and ranks among the top four counties nationally for
wind generation. He explained over the next 15 years, the county is expected to host 20+
large-scale RESS projects, generating an estimated €40 million or more in Community Benefit
Funds, including near-neighbour payments. He provided elected members a map of current and
planned windfarm projects. He highlighted the benefits of a Pooled fund and how it could work.
He provided a table of the governance structure along with the risks and mitigation.

He concluded by highlighted the next steps, including seeking Council feedback on the proposal,
engaging with community groups through the PPN, continuing discussions with energy
developers, refining governance based on stakeholder input, securing support from elected
representatives, and undertaking a fact-finding visit to the 9CC Group.

Cllr. J. Leahy, Cathaoirleach, thanked Mr. A. Hickey for his presentation. Before inviting
questions, he referred to Mr. E. Fennell, Meetings Administrator, who provided an advisory note
on the policy and procedures for in-committee meetings.

Cllr. J. Leahy, Cathaoirleach, informed Mr. A. Hickey that the elected members are supportive of
pooling Community Benefit Funds. He sought clarification on the proposed structure of the
fund, particularly the percentage allocated to the Near Neighbours Fund, noting the importance
of this allocation as it represents funding that is effectively unavailable for pooling.

In response, Mr. A. Hickey advised that approximately 50% of the fund is allocated to the Near
Neighbours Fund.

Cllr. J. Leahy, Cathaoirleach, sought clarification on the percentage of the fund to be allocated
to administration costs. He also requested an update on the expected timeframe for finalising
the report and making it available for presentation to local communities. The Cathaoirleach
emphasised the importance of progressing the report within the next four weeks, noting that
Oireachtas members are scheduled to meet shortly and that the Minister is aware the report is
forthcoming.

Mr. A. Hickey advised that administration costs would be capped at 10%. He noted, however,
that he could not confirm whether the final report could be completed within the next month.
Mr. A. Murray informed members that it was essential to ensure the proposed package is fully
refined before being presented to energy companies and existing communities to maximise the
likelihood of their opting in.

Cllr. F. McDonnell sought confirmation that, once finalised, the proposed package would be
brought back to the elected members for consideration before being presented to external
stakeholders and he wanted to ensure an in-depth analysis of the community schemes that are
in operation for the last 15 years and see if there is anything wrong with the current schemes.

In response Mr. A. Hickey advised that they would be bringing the proposed package back to
elected members and that an analysis was carried out on the current schemes. He informed
members that they met with Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment (DCEE) they
were receptive to what was discussed but it is important that we get them on side. He advised
the need to put the concept out there with communities on the ground and to see if we have
their support.

3|Page
Elected members thanked Mr. A. Hickey and Mr. A. Murray for their presentation. Cllr. N. Cribbin
expressed his support for the pooling of Community Benefit Funds, noting that a larger, combined
fund would enable the delivery of major projects such as the Edenderry swimming pool. He also
emphasised the need to continue supporting existing local initiatives, including Tidy Towns,
playgrounds and GAA clubs. Cllr. Cripbin added that, should the proposal to pool funds proceed,
he would like to see the application process simplified.

Members joined with Cllr. L. Quinn in emphasising the need for fairness in the allocation of funds,
noting that funding should be ring-fenced for communities within county boundaries. They
stressed that money generated in Offaly should remain in Offaly and highlighted the importance
of ensuring that the initiative supports the creation of well-paid local jobs.

Mr. E. Ryan, Chief Executive, advised that a body of work could be undertaken using GIS mapping
to identify the location of wind turbines and assess how much of the overall fund would fall within
Near Neighbour zones (1-2 km). He highlighted the importance of determining the potential
portion of the fund up to a maximum of 50% that may be allocated to Near Neighbours, noting
that this may need to be discussed with the Minister.

Mr. A. Murray confirmed that this work can be advanced.

Cllr. J. Leahy, Cathaoirleach, noted that two key actions now need to be progressed.

He advised that the first step is to identify the existing funds and engage with the relevant
committees to present the report and gather feedback. Ms. A. Dillon, DOS, asked whether
members serving on existing committees could assist with this engagement process.

He further noted the need to get feedback from the recent meeting with the Department of
Climate, Energy and the Environment (DCEE).

Clr. J. Leahy, Cathaoirleach, proposed that an online briefing be arranged for Members with Mr.
A. Hickey in approximately one month’s time, ahead of the next Council meeting.

Ms. A. Dillon, Director of Services, requested that Members currently serving on the relevant
committees assist in engaging with their respective groups.

2. Uisce Eireann Update

Mr. P. Mc Loughlin, Director of Service, provided the elected members with a short briefing on the
Community Benefit Fund with regard to the Eastern Midlands Water Supply Project. He advised
that a strong submission was prepared reflecting the elected members concerns.

Mr. P. McLoughlin advised on a number of key questions that were raised in relation to the
proposed Community Benefit Scheme.

1. Mr. McLoughlin noted that the value-based modelis linked to the overall construction cost
of the project. Based on mid-range cost estimates, the current fund equates to
approximately 0.142% of the construction cost proposed by Uisce Eireann. He also
highlighted the significant national economic value of the scheme, which is estimated at
€29.9 billion.

4|Page
At the request of the Chief Executive, it was proposed that the construction-cost model be
retained and that the contribution rate be increased to 0.5%. This adjustment would result
in a fund approximately three and a half times larger than the current proposal.

2. It was noted that if the scheme is to remain linked to construction costs, a weighted
allocation increase of 30% would be required. The Council outlined several factors
supporting this position, including:

e The County has the lowest disposable income of any host county.

e The highest projected impact, estimated at 50%.

e 53 public road crossings, three times more than any other county.

e Anestimated 300 km haul route.

e Six pipe storage locations.

e One booster station.

e A compressed construction programme, including electrical connections and
associated works.

3. The fund duration is currently proposed at 5 years. It has been requested that this be
extended to 10 years to bring it in line with comparable strategic infrastructure funds and
to provide communities with the necessary timeframe to deliver high-quality, high-impact
projects.

4. Itis also proposed that the maximum allocation per project be increased from €25,000 to
at least €100,000, to better support the delivery of meaningful and sustainable community
projects.

5. Offaly County Council expressed support for the principle that local authorities should act
as fund administrators. The Council also requested that the UE Fund designate the Local
Authority as the administrator of the Community Benefit Fund.

Cllr. P. Ormond thanked Mr. P. McLoughlin and acknowledged the work that went into preparing
the detailed report. He noted the proposal to assign an engineer to each Municipal District and
the intention to have a bond in place.

However, he expressed concern particularly in relation to South Offaly, where significant road
improvement works have already been carried out. With heavy traffic expected around the
depots, he highlighted that these roads are likely to deteriorate rapidly, causing inconvenience to
local residents who will experience the impact without receiving any direct benefit.

He asked where the funding will come from to continuously maintain and upgrade these roads
during the project, given the expected level of wear and tear.

Mr. P. McLoughlin explained that as the roads authority, the contractor will be operating under
licence from the Council, and the bond will allow the Council to take action immediately if any
issues arise.

He advised the main priority is the health and safety of road users, and the bond will ensure the
Council can respond quickly to any risks. It will also protect the annual roads budget by allowing
the Council to draw on the bond to repair or upgrade roads as required.

Cllr. J. Leahy suggested that a National Infrastructure Fund or similar national project may
ultimately supersede these arrangements, potentially making the process cost-neutral. He

5|Page
agreed with the points raised and noted that if the €8 million in development contributions were
to materialise, members would expect that it be ring-fenced, and that they would be permitted to
do so. He highlighted that the recent decision to remove the fixed split between roads and open
spaces in the Development Contribution Scheme provides greater flexibility in how these funds
may be allocated.

Mr. A. Murray reminded members that the allocation of development contributions is an
executive function.

3. Just Transition Fund Application Update

Mr. P. McLoughlin, Director of Services, briefed the Elected Members on the EU Just Transition
Fund applications, confirming that all proposed projects align with the Climate Action Plan. He
advised that seventeen expressions of Interest have been submitted and are currently under
consideration.

He outlined the project categories included in the submissions. In relation to Building Energy
Efficiency, seven projects have been put forward, comprising energy upgrades to libraries and
Municipal District offices. Under the Large Building Responsive Regeneration category, Birr
Courthouse has been identified as the single project proposed.

He outlined the Sustainable Mobility submissions, noting that three applications fall under this
heading: the Kilcormac Last Mile Project, Turraun Grand Canal Bridge, and the Tullamore Cycle
Network Phase which is a substantial scheme that is due to proceed to Part 8 shortly. He also
referred to a Sustainable Mobility Feasibility Study relating to the development of a multi-modal
transport hub adjacent to Tullamore Train Station, as well as the Midland Cycle Destination
proposal.

Minutes of 14 Meeting of Tipperary Local Community and Development
Committee held on Monday 21* March, 2016 at Littleton Community
Centre, Thurles.

Present:
Public Sector: Rita Guinan, Eileen Condon, Cllr. John Carroll, Adrian Cunneen,
Cllr. Joe Hannigan

Private Sector: Charles Stanley Smith (Chair), Isabel Cambie, Michael Murray,
Brian Cleary, Clare Cashman, Catherine Guest, Cora Horgan.

Apologises: -

Public Sector: Joe Mac Grath, Donal Mullane, Clir. Mary Hanna Hourigan,
Angela Joy

Private Sector: Sara Bourke, Tim Cullinane,

In attendance: Sinéad Carr, Margo Hayes, Breda O'Connor, Attracta Lyons.

The Chairperson welcomed the members and declared the meeting open. The
members agreed to take item No. 4 (Agreeing Strategic Operational Framework
for the LCDC) as the last item on the agenda. Apologies were noted

Confirmation of Minutes of Tipperary LCDC meeting — (21*' March, 2016)

The minutes of Tipperary LCDC dated 21*' March, 2016 were agreed; subject to
the following bullet point been added as a separate point;

e There is an inherent assumption that SICAP clients will all progress to
self-employment within a midyear and annual calendar year

And subject to the point below been noted:

e The lack of referrals by Department of Social Protection, Kilkenny in the
Ballingarry area

Proposed by: Isabel Cambie and Seconded by: Eileen Condon
Matters Arising:

> Sinéad Carr confirmed that a meeting with the Department of Social
Protection, both Local Development Companies and Local Enterprise
Office to take place shortly to agree on how to add value and enhance
existing services in the context of SICAP work and in particular the
referral process and self employment supports.

> Margo Hayes confirmed that a SICAP feedback template has been received
from the Paul Skinnader, Pobal and Ms. Hayes will complete this template on
behalf of the LCDC based on the Members recent feedback and discussion on
SICAP.

> Environmental Seat (LCDC) — Charles Stanley Smith confirmed that the

Ms. Ward Co-ordinator, PPN is working on filling the Environmental seat
on the LCDC. The environmental representative should be in place by
June. This was noted by the members.

Update on Local Development Strategy — A. Lyons

Attracta Lyons referred to the feedback document from the Independent
Selection Committee on the Local Development Strategy which was circulated
with the agenda. Following an extensive discussion on this matter it was
agreed to respond to the issues based on the report circulated by Ms. Lyons
prior to the meeting as follows:-

‘Evaluation Committees’ are in adherence with the Programme
Requirements. Current Draft Operating Rules state the Evaluation Committee
can be varied by area of specialisation (e.g. economic, social) but cannot be
divided by geographical location within the LDS area. To date LDCs have been
working on premise of two evaluation committees (operating on North & South
basis) so adherence with Operating Rules is therefore an issue

The Board of the Implementing Partner cannot review the recommendation of
the Evaluation Committee. This is understood but the Boards can note for
LAG's attention where they do not agree with recommendation of Evaluation
Committee (without clearly changing the recommendation of the Evaluation
committee) . Process for same has beed drafted in the current draft Service
level Agreement

Budget - The Programme budget needs to be appropriately aligned with the
timeframe of the LEADER Programme. In this context, the timeframe for the
delivery of actions may need to be reviewed. — Pobal has advised budget to end
of 2020 only so revision will involve allocation of funds from 2016 — 2020 (up to
five years). Budget originally submitted was based on a 6 year period. This has
implications for project spend and staffing levels.

Further detail on the local authority staff that are working on the LEADER
programme. will also be provided as Tipperary County Council personnel
providing LAG support and Financial Partner roles will be outlined in terms of
no., relevant qualification and experience, and previous direct experience of
LEADER Programme(s) will be submitted.

Additional detail on each of the following to be provided in terms of an
explanation or examples of types of projects that could be funded:-

Strategic Action 1.1: ‘Activity Tourism’

Strategic Action 1.4: 'Niche Accommodation’

Strategic Action 4.1: ‘Broadband’

Local Objective 7 ‘Development of Renewable energy’
Strategic Action 9.1 ‘Technica! Studies’.

Members will be advised of the changes at the April meeting.

th
Update on progress in development of the common templates (e.g.
application forms, assessment reports etc) — Isabel Cambie

Isabel Cambie confirmed to the meeting that considerable work has been
undertaken by both Local Development Companies on the RDP expression of
interest templates, promoter application forms, together with check list and
promotional templates. However, it was noted that the templates cannot be
finalised until the Operating Rules are agreed nationally. It is also proposed
that both Evaluation Committees will use the same documentation. It was
agreed that once the Operating Rules are near finalisation the Local
Development Companies will bring the final proposals to the LCDC for initial
approval. It was suggested that the sustainable communities sub group would
have a role to input into various RDP documentation and forms prior to them
being presented to the LCDC for approval. This was noted.

Correspondence:-

> Margo Hayes circulated a copy of the national LCDC logo it was noted
that a localised version will be available shortly to each Local Authority
citing the local authority area. Once the localised version is signed off it
will have to be used on all documentation and promotional material.

Ms. Carr referred to the upcoming SICAP Information event which is due
to take place on 4"" May in Gibson Hotel, Point Village, Dublin 1. This
workshop event is being rolled out by the Department of Environment for
Social Inclusion and Local Development Companies representatives on
the LCDC. This training would greatly benefit their respective roles in
overseeing the delivery of SICAP Programme. As places are limited to
three, it was agreed that the relevant members would contact Margo
Hayes to agree and select the nominees. This was noted

It was agreed that Attracta Lyons on behalf of the LCDC would raise the
matter of the animators being excluded for the current RDP programme.
It was recommended that Ms. Lyons would raise this matter at the next
national forum.

Margo Hayes confirmed that under the SICAP contract the LCDC
Members are obliged to be notified of staffing changes to the
programme. It was noted that Trish Purcell and Karolina Woznicka have
been appointed by North Tipperary Leader Partnership Ltd as part-time
Outreach Development Workers with SICAP.

Michael Murray informed the meeting that Michelle Putti, Programme
Manager, SICAP, NTLP Ltd will be leaving NTLP Ltd shortly to take up a
new position with St. Vincent de Paul with a regional function. Michael
Murray and the Chairman on behalf of the Members conveyed their good
wishes to Michelle Putti on her recent promotion. The Members thanked
Ms. Putti for her commitment and tremendous work on the SICAP
Programme and wished Ms. Putti every success and happiness in the
future. Mr. Murray confirmed that the recruitment process to replace Ms.
Puitti will commence shortly.
Date of next meeting

> It was agreed that the next meeting will take place at 10.00 a.m. on Monday
18" April, in Littleton Community Centre, Thurles.

> It was noted that Margo Hayes has sent a request to Information Technology
Section, Tipperary County Council to consider developing a LCDC web site.

It was also noted that Margo Hayes is now working on the Social Inclusion
Programme and Michael Moroney who also has a function with the Strategic
Project Unit has joined the LCDC Team and initially will take up responsibility
for the sustainable communities subcommittee.

Agreeing Strategic Operational Framework for LCDC — C Lynch, LIT

Ciaran Lynch presented and circulated a discussion paper on the “Strategic Role of the
LCDC’ ~ (attached as Appendix 1). Mr. Lynch outlined the function and purpose of the
LCDC and in its role acknowledges the need to have a strong strategic focus. Mr.
Lynch outlined that the LCDC is a strategic body and its focus needs to be on setting
high level outcomes and opportunities for funding.

The identification of the strategic steps need to:
> achieve those outcomes
> providing assistance to the implementation of those steps where requested
> monitoring of the extent to which the outcomes are achieved.

The LECP provides the framework for this.

Mr. Lynch also set out where the LCDC is given a remit to endorse decisions it should
make sure that the decisions and their rationale are clear. In some instances where an
organisation is subject to review/an audit by other(s), the LCDC should work with those
review and audit bodies where necessary and try to avoid duplication. Mr. Lynch
recommended that the LCDC could set out an operational work plan which identifies
the activities of the LCDC in its strategic and oversight role. The operational work plan
could include proactive and reactive actions as well as the agreed processes and
protocols. The operational work plan will ensure a good spread of activity and also
ensure that the key functions are been implemented together with avoiding duplication.

Following discussion by the Members on this item it was agreed to look at developing
an operational work plan for the LCDC. To engage and assist with the relevant
stakeholders based around the LECP to add and develop new funding opportunities

AGENDA ITEMS

Cathaoirleach Cllr. Liam Quinn welcomed everyone to the January monthly meeting and
wished everyone a Happy New Year.

1. Confirmation of Minutes from the December Meeting
It was proposed by Cllr. Eddie Fitzpatrick and seconded by Cllr. Fergus Mc Donnell
that the minutes of the monthly meeting held on 10° December 2025 be adopted.

Comhairle Chontae Uibh Fhaili
